RAW264.7 macrophages were stimulated with the purified recombinant protein for RNA sequencing. Seven proteins were retained as antigen sources, and the final construct contained seven HTL epitopes, five B-cell epitopes, and ten CTL epitopes. Immunized mice produced antigen-specific IgG, IgG1, and IgG2a, and antigen-restimulated splenocytes secreted higher levels of IFN-γ, IL-2, TNF-α, and IL-17. Vaccine-induced antibodies recognized both the recombinant protein and components present in MAP lysate while showing limited reactivity toward the bovine tuberculosis diagnostic antigen PPD, and sequence analysis predicted no substantial similarity between the construct and the diagnostic antigens ESAT-6, CFP-10, MPB70, and MPB83, supporting potential DIVA compatibility. In macrophages, recombinant-protein stimulation changed gene-expression profiles and enriched pathways related to cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, NF-κB, TNF, IL-17, Toll-like receptor, and NOD-like receptor signaling. The construct was immunogenic in mice; the exploratory MYY-containing formulation showed numerically higher immune-response readouts in this experimental setting, although these differences were not statistically significant. This adjuvant-associated observation requires further validation, and protection against MAP infection still needs to be tested in challenge experiments and target animals.

title: Sophocarpine Inhibits Proliferation and Triggers Apoptosis in Breast Cancer Cells by Modulating the miR-21/PTEN/AKT and ERK1/2 Signaling Networks.
abstract: Background: Sophocarpine (SC), a tetracyclic quinolizidine alkaloid, has shown antitumor potential, yet its activity and underlying mechanisms in breast cancer remain unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the anticancer effects of SC and the molecular mechanism, focusing on the involvement of microRNA-21 (miR-21) and AKT/mTOR and ERK1/2 signaling networks. Methods: In MDA-MB-231 and T-47D breast cancer cells, SC cytotoxicity and growth-inhibitory effects were evaluated using MTT viability, colony formation, migration assays, and flow cytometry for cell cycle and apoptosis analysis. RT-qPCR analysis, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining were performed to measure RNA and protein expression, respectively. Molecular docking analysis was performed to explore SC's interaction with the miR-21 precursor. Results: SC treatment effectively inhibited the proliferation, survival, and migration of breast cancer cells. It also induced cell cycle arrest and triggered apoptosis in both cell lines. Mechanistically, SC downregulated oncogenic miR-21 transcription, thereby enhancing tumor suppressors PTEN and PDCD4 and suppressing AKT/mTOR and ERK1/2 signaling. Interestingly, restoration of miR-21 reversed SC's effects on PTEN and PDCD4, confirming SC's miR-21 dependency. Docking analysis suggested that SC may bind the miR-21 precursor and interfere with its maturation. SC also increased long noncoding RNA GAS5 while reducing miR-196a-5p and HIF-1α transcripts. It shifted the Bcl2/Bax/Bad/caspases balance toward apoptosis. Conclusions: These findings identify SC as a potential structural scaffold exhibiting preliminary anti-tumor activity against breast cancer cells, at least in part, through modulating miR-21 and inhibition of the AKT/mTOR/ERK1/2 survival network.

title: Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals Hormonal, miRNA-Associated, and NLR-Linked Aphid Defense in Lycium barbarum.
abstract: Aphid infestation constrains goji berry production, yet its defense architecture remains poorly resolved. We integrated comparative transcriptomics, phytohormone profiling, small RNA sequencing, and genome-wide nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) analysis to dissect aphid defense in Lycium barbarum (cv. Ningqi-10)and susceptible L. chinense. Aphid bioassays confirmed that L. barbarum imposes a significant fitness cost on aphids, reducing survival, longevity, and fecundity. Transcriptomic comparison revealed fewer but more defense-enriched differentially expressed genes in the resistant accession. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified a stress-associated turquoise module (288 genes, r = 0.981) receptor-like kinases and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) components, bridging extracellular signals sensing and hormone signaling. Phytohormone profiling showed that salicylic acid (SA) accumulated to 72 h, whereas jasmonic acid (JA) peaked transiently at 24 h, producing an increased SA/JA ratio suggesting a shift to SA-dominated signaling. MiR398a-3p and miR319-3p dynamics coincided with this SA/JA shift, suggesting a possible link to hormone-coordinated regulation and candidate targets for validation. NLR analysis identified 151 candidate genes, including 18 L. barbarum-biased NLRs up-regulation under SA-dominated signaling, implying a link to SA signaling. Collectively, these findings support a multi-layered framework integrating SA signaling, transcriptional reprogramming, and coupled miRNA and NLR responses in aphid defense.

title: From Target Discovery to Spatial Delivery: A Translational Roadmap for Gene-Targeted Therapies in Glioma.
abstract: Diffuse gliomas are increasingly defined by molecular alterations, yet the clinical translation of gene-targeted therapies remains constrained by a persistent mismatch between target biology and spatial pharmacology. In this review, we connect target discovery to clinical development by integrating spatial and longitudinal tumor biology with payload selection, delivery engineering, biomarker design, manufacturing, and mechanism-driven trials. Recent clinical practices in locoregional CAR-T cells, oncolytic and gene-delivery viruses, tumor-homing myeloid cell gene therapy, mutation- and neoantigen-directed vaccination, RNA nanomedicines, and emerging genome-editing strategies suggest that vehicle and route of administration dramatically change drug exposure, therapeutic index, immune activity, and resistance. We therefore propose the concept of "delivery-adjusted targetability," in which a candidate target is judged not only by biological dependency but also by clonality, longitudinal stability, normal-brain expression, anatomical distribution, modality compatibility, and achievable target engagement. We further argue that the clinically actionable unit in diffuse glioma is often a target-anatomical compartment pair rather than a molecular target considered in isolation. Moreover, we advocate target-payload-vehicle-route-biomarker co-design and a stage-gated evidence package. This framework provides a potential way to compare otherwise dissimilar platforms, distinguish target failure from delivery failure, and reject biologically attractive but spatially implausible programs earlier. Treating molecular dependency and spatial access as a single design problem can make precision neuro-oncology more experimentally falsifiable and clinically actionable.

title: Inhalable Plant Exosome-like Nanoparticles from Houttuynia cordata Ameliorate Acute Lung Injury via Redox Modulation and Immune Reprogramming.
abstract: Background: Acute lung injury (ALI) features oxidative stress, macrophage dysfunction, and barrier disruption, with limited safe therapies. Plant-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (PENs) delivered noninvasively to the lung are promising but understudied. Methods: In vitro, HELNs were evaluated for their ability to scavenge ROS, restore mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) modulate M1/M2 polarization, and suppress pro-inflammatory cytokines. RNA-seq was also used to evaluate the TNF/NOD-like pathway and mitochondrial-related gene expression. In vivo, the evaluated parameters included biodistribution, therapeutic outcomes (lung wet/dry weight ratio, BALF protein concentration, MPO and MDA levels, histology), immune cell profiles, and cytokines. Biosafety was assessed via hematology, serum biochemistry, and histology. Results: In vitro, HELNs acted dose-dependently by scavenging ROS, recovering MMP, promoting M2 and suppressing M1 polarization, and reducing TNF-α, IL-6 release. Additionally, RNA-seq confirmed downregulation of TNF/NOD-like signals and regulated mitochondrial gene expression. In vivo, nebulized HELNs preferentially accumulated in inflamed lungs, with significantly higher pulmonary retention than intravenous delivery. HELNs reduced lung wet/dry weight ratio, BALF protein, MPO and MDA levels, and histological injury scores; decreased neutrophils and CD4+/CD8+ T cells; increased alveolar macrophages and Tregs; and lowered TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6. No significant systemic toxicity was observed. Conclusions: Nebulized HELNs offer a safe, effective, noninvasive ALI therapy by disrupting the oxidative stress-inflammation vicious cycles, reprogramming pulmonary immunity, and restoring barrier integrity, with strong translational potential.

title: Genome-Wide Identification and Analysis of the Perennial Ryegrass (Lolium perenne L.) WRKY Family Associated with Heat Stress.
abstract: Perennial ryegrass, the most widely cultivated forage and turfgrass, exhibits a relatively poor temperature tolerance, which restricts its distribution and utilization in warmer regions. WRKY transcription factors regulate diverse biological processes in plants, including development and stress responses. Here, we report the comprehensive identification of 97 WRKY genes (LpWRKYs) in perennial ryegrass. The LpWRKYs were unevenly distributed across seven chromosomes, with one gene anchored to a scaffold. These genes were classified into three major groups and five subgroups based on phylogenetic relationships and structural domain diversity. All LpWRKYs contained either one or two WRKY domains and the LpWRKYs within the same group had similar motif compositions. A total of 12 tandem duplicates and 27 segmental duplicates were identified, suggesting that gene duplication might have contributed to the expansion of the LpWRKY gene family. Ka/Ks analysis revealed that all duplicated LpWRKY gene pairs were subjected to purifying selection during the evolution. Co-linearity analysis showed strong co-linearity between LpWRKYs and OsWRKYs from rice. Cis-acting elements in the LpWRKY promoters were related to growth and development, phytohormone responses, and stress responses. RNA-seq and qRT-PCR analysis revealed that the expression levels of LpWRKY5/16/33/35 were significantly up-regulated, while LpWRKY21/92 were significantly down-regulated in roots under heat stress. Additionally, LpWRKY12/21/33/35/43/89/92/96 displayed significant down-regulation in leaves under heat stress. It was suggested that these LpWRKYs were potentially associated with the heat-stress response in perennial ryegrass. Notably, LpWRKY33 and LpWRKY35 exhibited distinct tissue-specific transcriptional patterns in response to heat stress, implying their participation in complex tissue-dependent regulatory networks. Protein interaction prediction further suggested that LpWRKY96 may function as a potential central regulator in the heat response signaling network. Taken together, this study provides clues into the regulatory roles of the WRKY gene family in perennial ryegrass.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Biochemical Analyses Reveal Coordinated Suppression of ER-Associated Survival Signaling and Activation of ROS-Mediated Stress Responses by Oxidized Graphene Quantum Dots in Estrogen Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer.
abstract: Oxidized graphene quantum dots (o-GQDs) alter viability and cell-cycle progression in breast cancer cells, yet the cellular programs underlying these effects remain incompletely defined. We exposed MCF-7 cells to 10 mg/L o-GQD for 72 h and integrated RNA sequencing with quantitative protein-marker, ROS, antioxidant-intervention, proteasome-inhibition, and puromycin-labeling analyses from independent experiments. Transcriptomic analyses showed significant negative enrichment of proliferative and cell-cycle programs (E2F Targets, G2M Checkpoint, MYC Targets V1), with complementary KEGG/Reactome evidence of attenuated estrogen-associated programs. Quantitative Western blotting showed dose-dependent reductions in ERα (to 41.36 ± 13.73% at 10 mg/L), p-RB (to 8.31 ± 10.39%), and Survivin (to 23.97 ± 19.01%), with p-ERK/ERK attenuation and marked γ-H2AX accumulation (345.21 ± 161.39%). The ROS-positive fraction rose from 6.86% to 30.46%; antioxidant co-treatment failed to rescue the phenotype and MG132 did not consistently restore protein markers, arguing against oxidative stress or proteasomal degradation as standalone drivers. Reduced puromycin labeling added a protein-homeostasis readout consistent with reduced nascent protein synthesis. BT-474 and MDA-MB-231 cells showed weaker or different marker responses. Together, these findings define a coordinated MCF-7 response spanning estrogen-associated and cell-cycle programs, survival markers, protein homeostasis, and cell fate.

title: Evaluation of Two Combined Analytical Approaches to Assess the Impact of Rare Variants on Severe COVID-19.
abstract: Severe COVID-19 displays substantial inter-individual variability that cannot be fully explained by common genetic variants, suggesting a contribution of rare functional variation. We performed whole-genome sequencing in 191 Italian patients (96 moderate, 95 severe) to investigate rare coding variants (minor allele frequency <1% and <5%) via complementary network-based and machine learning approaches. Classical single-variant and burden tests did not identify significant associations after multiple testing correction. However, Network-based Heterogeneity Clustering (NHC) revealed that multiple gene clusters were enriched in severe cases, particularly those involving RNA polymerase II-mediated transcription, RNA metabolism, and vesicle-mediated transport pathways. Gene-level rare variant analysis via the variable threshold method identified five genes significantly associated with severe disease (FDR < 0.05), namely, EIF4G3, GTF2F2, LY96, COX6A1, and STK11, which are involved in transcriptional and translational regulation, innate immune signaling, and mitochondrial function. Unsupervised biclustering significantly stratified patients by severity, and a decision tree model highlighted the burden of DOCK10 variants as a key discriminator between phenotypes. Convergence between the network-based and machine learning results further supported the robustness of the identified signals. Overall, our integrative framework underscores the contribution of rare variants to COVID-19 severity and highlights the coordinated perturbation of interconnected molecular pathways as a determinant of clinical outcome.

title: Serum Proteomic Profiling by SomaScan Aptamer Array Identifies Candidate Predictive and Monitoring Biomarkers of Distant Recurrence in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks a blood-based biomarker for predicting or monitoring distant recurrence. We profiled 39 serum samples from 38 women (10 healthy controls; 12 non-recurrent [NR]; eight diagnosis-timepoint samples from patients who later recurred [DR-DIG]; nine recurrence-timepoint samples [DR-REC]) using the SomaScan v5.0 aptamer platform). Public tumor-tissue transcriptomic cohorts were used for supportive and exploratory analyses. No protein reached a false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05 for NR vs. DR-DIG; granzyme A (GZMA) and endoplasmic reticulum aminopeptidase 1 (ERAP1) showed the strongest nominal signals. For DR-DIG vs. DR-REC, 38 aptamers (37 proteins) reached FDR < 0.05, enriched for RNA-binding and nuclear-envelope proteins; this signature was retained in leave-one-out and storage-adjusted analyses. Higher GZMA mRNA was associated with longer recurrence-free survival in two independent cohorts (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.795, p = 0.018; HR = 0.186, p = 0.0057). Monitor genes showed near-chance concordance with metastatic tissue, and the source of the signature could not be resolved. An exploratory four-gene elastic-net panel reached a concordance index of 0.613 internally but 0.559 externally. GZMA is a candidate serum biomarker of TNBC recurrence risk, and the monitor signature is a preliminary observation. Both require protein-level validation in independent, prospectively collected serum cohorts.

title: Evolutionary and Functional Conservation of Topologically Associating Domain Boundaries in Rice Genomes.
abstract: Traditional evolutionary analysis has relied primarily on one-dimensional (1D) sequencing data, but recent advances in three-dimensional (3D) genomics allow for deeper investigation of how genome architecture shapes evolutionary divergence. In this study, we analyze conserved and species-specific topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries across multiple Oryza species to uncover both structural and functional evolutionary insights. Here, we characterize boundary conservation at different levels, from highly conserved to species-unique. We apply TCBF, a relatively novel and underutilized tool for TAD boundary conservation analysis, alongside a suite of complementary analyses, including gene ontology, RNA-seq, sequence conservation, and epigenetic profiling. Our approach not only validates canonical evolutionary relationships reflected in sequence data but also novel patterns unique to 3D genome organization. Most notably, our study uncovers strong associations between highly conserved TAD boundaries and RNA metabolism-related genes, as well as other genetic and epigenetic signatures, and a contrasting absence in minimally conserved boundaries. To our knowledge, we created the first phylogenetic reconstruction derived from topological domain data in plants, which demonstrated a strong similarity between 3D and 1D genomic evolutionary relationships. Overall, our work presents an approach that integrates the 3D genome structure into evolutionary genomics, addressing a critical and underexplored dimension of comparative plant genomics.

title: Precision Therapeutics for Monogenic Epilepsies: From Molecular Mechanisms to Disease Modification in Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies and Neurodevelopmental Disorders with Epilepsy.
abstract: Background: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) and neurodevelopmental disorders with epilepsy (NDD-E) are etiologically heterogeneous conditions historically treated with syndrome-based, symptomatic approaches. Advances in genomic sequencing have identified monogenic causes across more than 900 genes, creating opportunities for mechanism-informed and disease-modifying precision therapies. Methods: For this narrative review, PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through September 2026 using disorder-, gene-, mechanism-, and therapeutic-modality-specific terms to identify mechanism-informed and disease-modifying therapies for monogenic DEEs and NDD-E. Results: Pathogenic mechanisms include gain- or loss-of-function ion-channel abnormalities, altered neurotransmitter receptor/transporter function, impaired synaptic signaling, dysregulated intracellular pathways, metabolic deficiencies, protein misfolding, and transcriptional or epigenetic dysregulation. Across genes such as SCN1A, SCN2A, SCN8A, KCNQ2, KCNT1, KCNA2, CACNA1A, GABA-receptor subunits, SLC6A1, GRIN genes, SYNGAP1, STXBP1, DNM1, SHANK3, TSC1/TSC2, GNAO1, UBE3A, MECP2, and TCF4, therapeutic strategies range from repurposed and mechanism-targeted pharmacologic agents (e.g., sodium- and potassium-channel modulators, mTOR inhibitors) to antisense oligonucleotides, RNA interference, gene replacement or augmentation, transcriptional activation, and genome editing. Several programs have advanced from preclinical proof of concept into early- and late-phase human trials, with variant-specific functional classification increasingly guiding therapy selection, particularly distinguishing gain-of-function from loss-of-function disease. Conclusions: Precision therapeutics are shifting the treatment paradigm for monogenic DEEs and NDD-E from empiric seizure control toward mechanism-based targeting of dysregulated molecular pathways and gene-based disease-modifying therapies. Realizing this potential will require functional variant classification, delivery technologies capable of durable and cell-appropriate target engagement, and trial designs incorporating developmental and biomarker outcomes beyond seizure frequency alone to demonstrate genuine disease modification.

title: Identification of Genes Encoding Seminal Fluid Proteins in Coccinella septempunctata and Functional Analysis of the Gene Encoding Trypsin.
abstract: In this study, transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were used to identify genes encoding seminal fluid proteins in Coccinella septempunctata L. A total of 65 SFPs domains containing secretory signal peptides were identified, including trypsin, Kazal_2, His_Phos_2, Peptidase_M14, lipase, Kunitz_BPTI, Ribonuc_2-5A, and Gly-co_transf_90; an additional 22 signal peptide-containing domains were identified that lacked annotations in the Pfam database. Transcript levels of the 65 SFPs accounted for 87.58% of the total expression levels of 211 specifically expressed proteins in the male reproductive tract (MRT). RNA interference (RNAi) was used to analyze the function of the SFP trypsin. RNAi-mediated knockdown of the seminal fluid trypsin gene in male C. septempunctata, followed by mating with females, significantly reduced female fecundity and egg hatching rates. This study enriches our knowledge of insect SFPs and provides a theoretical basis for the artificial rearing of C. septempunctata.

title: SEMA3A in Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy: Exogenous Activity, Endogenous Regulation, and the MicroRNA Hypothesis.
abstract: Proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) remains a leading cause of surgical failure after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) repair. Although PVR involves multiple cell types and signaling pathways, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and related plasticity of retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells are major contributors to fibrocellular membrane formation and contraction. Semaphorin 3A (SEMA3A) has therefore attracted interest as a potential negative regulator of these pathogenic RPE responses. Recombinant SEMA3A inhibits RPE migration and proliferation and attenuates experimental PVR when administered at model induction. Yet this benefit does not establish that endogenous SEMA3A transcript levels are reduced. Published Source Data from a mouse model of traumatic PVR show significantly increased endogenous Sema3a transcript levels in RPE preparations compared with controls. The question is therefore why PVR progresses despite increased endogenous Sema3a transcript levels in this model. Possible explanations include microRNA-mediated translational repression, altered protein processing or secretion, reduced extracellular availability, and impaired NRP1/plexin signaling. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are particularly relevant because they can reduce protein output without a parallel decline in mRNA and can regulate multiple features of RPE EMT. This narrative review examines current evidence for SEMA3A in PVR, summarizes miRNA regulation of RPE EMT and related PVR phenotypes, and evaluates direct and indirect evidence for miRNA-SEMA3A interactions. We also compare the miRNA hypothesis with alternative explanations for inadequate endogenous SEMA3A activity and consider its implications for ocular biomarkers and target-site-selective RNA therapy. Current evidence makes miRNA-mediated regulation of SEMA3A a plausible and testable mechanism, although a causal role has yet to be demonstrated in RPE cells or PVR.

title: Isochlorogenic Acid C Mitigates CCl4-Induced Kidney Ferroptosis, Inflammation, and Fibrogenesis in Mice: Involvement of the SESN2/MAPKs and Hippo Pathways.
abstract: Renal damage is closely related to oxidative stress, inflammation, ferroptosis, and fibrosis. Renal fibrosis is closely related to oxidative stress, inflammation, and ferroptosis. Isochlorogenic acid C (IaC) has been demonstrated to have a protective effect against kidney injury in both in vivo and in vitro studies. Nonetheless, it remains uncertain whether IaC can mitigate kidney dysfunction induced by carbon tetrachloride (CCl4). In this study, we examined the protective effects of IaC on renal inflammation, ferroptosis, and fibrosis, as well as the underlying regulatory mechanisms. An experimental model of kidney injury was developed using ICR mice (in vivo) and HK-2 cells (in vitro), which were treated with CCl4 or TGFβ1. Gene/protein expressions were detected using RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry assays. In addition, to identify the potential mechanisms involved in this process, we conducted RNA interference and signaling pathway inhibition analysis. IaC alleviated CCl4-induced renal dysfunction and fibrosis. It resulted in the down-regulation of fibrosis-associated markers, specifically collagen I and α-SMA. Furthermore, IaC mitigated CCl4-induced renal inflammation by reducing the activities of TNF-α, IL-6, and NF-κB p65. IaC led to an up-regulation in the activities of GSH, SOD, and GPx in the renal tissues of mice. IaC effectively inhibited the elevation of renal ferroptosis-associated markers induced by CCl4, as evidenced by the reduced Fe2+ levels and the increased expression of GSH, GPX4, and SLC7A11. Moreover, IaC significantly enhanced the activation of Sestrin2 (SESN2). IaC resulted in a down-regulation of the expression levels of TGFβ1, YAP, TAZ, p-ERK, p-JNK, and p-p38 in the kidneys. Furthermore, IaC demonstrated an inhibitory effect on inflammation and fibrosis within an in vitro model of TGFβ-induced fibrosis. However, treatment with the inhibitors of MAPKs and YAP significantly enhanced the effects of IaC in TGFβ-stimulated HK-2 cells. Sestrin2 silencing also reversed the effects of IaC in TGFβ-stimulated HK-2 cells. IaC demonstrated effective docking with the active sites of the target proteins SESN2, GPX4, and YAP, thereby corroborating the predicted compatibility of interactions between IaC and these proteins. Our study demonstrates that IaC ameliorates CCl4-induced renal inflammation and fibrosis through modulation of the Hippo pathway and the SESN2/MAPKs pathways. IaC is a promising natural compound that can be used to treat kidney damage.

title: Circular RNAs in Alzheimer's Disease: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and EPAC Signalling in Ferroptosis.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and complex pathogenesis, involving amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, tau pathology, and neuroinflammation, driven by microglial shifts toward pro-inflammatory M1-like states, causing neuronal dysfunction and death, particularly by ferroptosis. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain limited, highlighting the need for novel molecular regulators. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), representing promising regulatory molecules and peripheral biomarkers. Evidence suggests that circRNAs regulate AD-related pathways, through microRNA (miRNA) sponging, including modulation of NF-κB/BACE1-dependent (nuclear-factor-kappa-B/beta-site APP-cleaving enzyme 1) amyloidogenic APP (amyloid precursor protein) processing and through disruption of NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) receptor-dependent synaptic signaling, exemplified by circRIMS2-driven UBE2K (ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2K)-mediated GluN2B (glutamate ionotropic receptor NMDA type subunit-2B) degradation. Additionally, circRNAs represent promising non-invasive diagnostic biomarkers. Plasma hsa_circRNA_050263 showed high diagnostic accuracy for early-stage AD. CircRNAs may offer a therapeutic strategy for modulating cell-death pathways, particularly ferroptosis. Selectively targeting EPAC2 (exchange protein directly activated by cAMP2) may preserve EPAC2-associated neuroprotection, while limiting EPAC1-associated ferroptosis, although challenges such as blood-brain barrier delivery remain to be addressed. This review summarizes circRNA biogenesis, diagnostic potential, and roles in AD pathogenesis, and limitations and AD models, besides investigating the selective circRNA-EPAC axis.

title: CircRNAs and Erectile Dysfunction: A Hybrid Review of Possible Interactions.
abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is a prevalent condition involving multiple molecular mechanisms. Although non-coding RNAs have emerged as important regulators of gene expression, the role of circular RNAs (circRNAs) in ED remains poorly defined. CircRNAs are characterised by a covalently closed loop structure that confers enhanced stability and enables diverse regulatory functions. This review aims to investigate the potential interactions between circRNAs and the signalling pathways linked to ED. Only two primary studies directly investigating circRNA dysregulation in ED were identified, highlighting the early stage of this field. This hybrid systematic narrative review combines a PRISMA-guided systematic search with a pre-specified, hypothesis-generating narrative synthesis of the broader circRNA literature across key signalling pathways implicated in ED, including the NO/cGMP/PKG, RhoA/ROCK, JNK/c-Jun/Bak, and TNF-α/NF-κB axes. We identify several circRNAs as potential regulators of endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and smooth muscle contractility. CircRNAs therefore emerge as candidate biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Given that direct evidence is currently limited to two animal studies, with no circRNA validated in human tissue or as a biomarker, these molecules should be regarded only as candidates for future biomarker and therapeutic target validation.

title: Regional Expression Profiles of Artemin Protein and GFRα3 mRNA During Postnatal Brain Development in Rats.
abstract: Artemin, a member of the glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor family, plays important roles in neuronal processes through GDNF family receptor alpha 3 (GFRα3)-mediated signaling. However, the expression patterns of Artemin and GFRα3 during normal postnatal brain development remain poorly characterized. This study characterized regional Artemin protein and Gfra3 messenger RNA (mRNA) expression profiles in the rat brain at distinct stages of postnatal development. Male Wistar rats aged 9, 41, and 70 days (n = 10/group) were examined. Artemin levels were quantified in the prefrontal cortex, striatum, and cerebellum using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), whereas Gfra3 mRNA expression was determined by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Regional and age-related differences were evaluated statistically. No significant age-related differences in Artemin levels were observed within any brain region. However, cerebellar Artemin levels were significantly higher than those in the prefrontal cortex and striatum across all age groups. Age-related changes in Gfra3 mRNA expression were detected only in the cerebellum, where expression was significantly higher in 41-day-old rats than in both 9- and 70-day-old rats and was also significantly higher in 70-day-old rats than in 9-day-old rats. Regional differences in Gfra3 mRNA expression were detected only in 41-day-old rats, with significantly higher expression in the cerebellum than in the prefrontal cortex and striatum. These findings provide, to our knowledge, the first comprehensive characterization of Artemin protein and Gfra3 mRNA expression at distinct stages of normal postnatal brain development and highlight the cerebellum as a region characterized by consistently higher Artemin levels and developmentally variable Gfra3 mRNA expression, supporting further investigation of Artemin-GFRα3 signaling in this region during postnatal brain development.

title: Comparative DIA Proteomics of Neuroblastoma: Laser-Microdissected FFPE Tumors Versus Cell Lines.
abstract: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor specimens are widely available and represent a valuable resource for retrospective cancer research; however, chemical cross-linking has historically limited their application in proteomic studies. In this study, we developed a proteomic workflow for laser-microdissected FFPE neuroblastoma tissues and evaluated their biological characteristics in comparison with established neuroblastoma cell lines. Tumor regions were isolated from FFPE sections by laser microdissection, and protein profiles were analyzed using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. Seven high-risk neuroblastoma FFPE samples and four neuroblastoma cell lines were examined. A total of 4511 proteins were identified in FFPE tissues and 6812 proteins in cell lines, with 4311 proteins shared between both systems. After quality filtering, 2186 proteins were retained for downstream quantitative analyses. Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering demonstrated clear separation between FFPE tissues and cell lines despite a strong overall correlation in mean protein abundance across the quantified proteome. Differential abundance and functional enrichment analyses revealed distinct proteomic features between the two systems. Proteins enriched in FFPE tissues were associated with extracellular vesicles, the extracellular space, the cornified envelope, intermediate filament organization and cell junctions. In contrast, proteins enriched in neuroblastoma cell lines were associated with RNA binding, translation, rRNA processing, oxidative phosphorylation, and glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, reflecting enhanced biosynthetic and metabolic activity. Together, these findings demonstrate that FFPE tissues and neuroblastoma cell lines capture complementary aspects of neuroblastoma biology, supporting their combined use as a comprehensive framework for biomarker discovery and translational research in pediatric oncology.

title: Comparative Transcriptomic Profiling of Diabetic Wound Responses to Recombinant Periplaneta americana Thymosin Isoforms in Male ob/ob Mice.
abstract: Background: Preparations derived from Periplaneta americana, such as Kangfuxin Liquid, have been used in China for wound and ulcer management, yet their active constituents remain incompletely characterized. Recombinant P. americana thymosin isoforms (Pa-THYs) have been reported to accelerate wound closure in nondiabetic mice. Their effects and associated transcriptional responses in diabetic wounds remain unclear. Methods: Three Pa-THYs (THY1-3) were topically applied to full-thickness excisional wounds in ob/ob diabetic mice, with thymosin β4 (Tβ4) and PBS used as positive and negative controls. Wound healing was assessed by planimetry, hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, Masson trichrome staining, and CD31 immunohistochemistry. RNA sequencing of wound tissues on days 3 and 8 post-injury was performed, followed by differential gene expression analysis, Gene Ontology and pathway enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction network construction, marker gene-based cell-type-associated expression scoring, and preranked GSEA. Results: On day 8, mean wound-closure percentages ranged from 95% to 97% across the THY1, THY2, THY3, and Tβ4 groups compared to 81% in the PBS group. At this time point, treated wounds showed more complete epithelial coverage. The CD31-positive area fraction was higher in all active-treatment groups, whereas the collagen volume fraction was higher in the THY2 and THY3 groups than in the PBS group. Among the Pa-THY groups, THY2 showed the largest day-3 DEG set, whereas THY1 and THY3 showed prominent epithelial-differentiation signatures at the later time point. THY3 showed the largest day-8 DEG set and the greatest pairwise DEG overlap with Tβ4. As a complementary threshold-independent analysis, GSEA identified coordinated early metabolic responses, broadly distributed interferon-associated enrichment, and late keratinization enrichment in THY1, THY3, and Tβ4. Conclusions: Topical THY1, THY2, and THY3 improved day-8 wound closure in male ob/ob mice, with accompanying changes in epithelial coverage, CD31-positive area fractions, and collagen staining. The transcriptomic findings indicate shared pathway-level responses together with time- and isoform-associated differences. These results support a further preclinical evaluation of Pa-THYs.

title: Long-Read Evidence for Repeat-Associated Structural Heterogeneity in the Mitochondrial Genome of Rhododendron spinuliferum.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Plant mitochondrial genomes are structurally dynamic, and assembled paths may not reflect all molecular configurations. We characterized the mitochondrial genome of Rhododendron spinuliferum and evaluated repeat-associated structural heterogeneity and transcript support for mitochondrial RNA processing. Methods: Public PacBio HiFi reads were assembled and curated; Illumina reads from a second individual provided cross-individual sequence support. Candidate local connections were assessed by strict single-read two-junction phasing. Gene content, repeats, plastid-derived sequences, comparative genomics, phylogeny, predicted C-to-U RNA-editing sites, and mature exon junctions were also examined. Results: Three representative assembly paths totaled 786,593 bp and contained 32 protein-coding loci, three rRNA genes, and 19 tRNA types. A total of 226 HiFi reads supported four local configurations associated with two repeat pairs, and all four persisted across 24 filtering combinations. Nine mitochondrial plastid DNA transfer blocks covered 6.77 kb. Public RNA-seq data provided read-level support for 211 of 475 predicted editing sites and all 12 examined mature exon junctions of nad1, nad2, and nad5. Across six congeners, 99.7% of resolved homologous positions corresponding to RNA-supported sites retained genomic C. Conclusions: These results support repeat-associated local structural heterogeneity in the R. spinuliferum mitogenome and provide a curated DNA- and RNA-supported resource for comparative Rhododendron mitochondrial genomics.

title: Genome-Wide Identification of the PP2A Gene Family in Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa) and Pharmacological Evidence for the Involvement of PP2A in ALA-Mediated Salt Tolerance.
abstract: Background: Protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) is a conserved serine/threonine phosphatase that plays crucial roles in stress responses, yet its function in strawberry (Fragaria spp.) remains largely uncharacterized. This study aimed to characterize the PP2A gene family in octoploid strawberry and to investigate its involvement in ALA-induced salt tolerance. Methods: We identified PP2A genes in the octoploid strawberry 'Benihoppe' genome and classified them into scaffold (A), regulatory (B55, B56, B″), and catalytic (C) subunit families. Segmental duplication and selection pressure were analyzed using Ka/Ks. Time-course RNA-seq was performed under NaCl and ALA treatments. Physiological assays measured SOD and CAT activities, O2•- and MDA accumulation, and PP2A activity. Cantharidin was used to pharmacologically inhibit PP2A. Results: Seventy-five PP2A genes were identified. Segmental duplication was the primary driver of PP2A family expansion (70/75 genes), with all duplicated pairs under strong purifying selection (mean Ka/Ks = 0.138). Time-course RNA-seq analysed with DESeq2 identified three B56-subfamily PP2A genes as differentially expressed between NaCl and NaCl + ALA at 24 h (FDR < 0.05), the most strongly affected being FaPP2AB'η-5; in contrast, several C4 catalytic subunits were suppressed by salt stress. This ALA-responsive induction declined sharply at 48 h and 72 h. Physiological assays demonstrated that ALA significantly enhanced SOD and CAT activities while reducing O2•- and MDA accumulation under NaCl stress, and ALA also elevated PP2A activity. Cantharidin largely attenuated both the ALA-induced increase in PP2A activity and ALA-mediated antioxidant protection. Conclusions: This study provides a comprehensive characterization of the strawberry PP2A gene family and indicates that PP2A activity contributes to ALA-induced salt tolerance, revealing a functional link between ALA signaling and PP2A-mediated antioxidant defense.

title: Aberrant mRNA 5-methylcytosine modification contributes to ovarian dysfunction in a rat model of polycystic ovary syndrome.
abstract: This study investigated the altered landscape of messenger RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C) methylation and the functional involvement of m5C-related regulators in a rat model of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). A PCOS rat model was established by dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) induction, with the phenotype confirmed through estrous cycle monitoring, serum sex hormone analysis, and ovarian morphological assessment. Differentially m5C-methylated mRNAs were identified using an m5C epitranscriptomic microarray, and their associated biological pathways were predicted by KEGG analysis. Global m5C methylation levels and the expression and m5C enrichment of selected pathway-related genes were validated in ovarian tissues and isolated primary ovarian granulosa cells using dot blot, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and methylated RNA immunoprecipitation quantitative PCR (MeRIP-qPCR). The functional roles of TET2 and NSUN6 were further evaluated using shRNA-mediated knockdown, followed by analysis of PI3K/AKT-related signaling proteins, serum sex hormones, and ovarian histopathology. m5C modifications were predominantly localized within coding sequences and 3' untranslated regions. Among 1,090 RNAs showing both differential m5C methylation and expression, 36 genes exhibited significant correlations between methylation and expression changes. Global mRNA m5C methylation was significantly elevated in the PCOS group. The m5C-related regulators Nsun6 and Tet2 showed increased m5C enrichment and significantly elevated protein expression. KEGG analysis linked the differentially modified transcripts to endocrine resistance and insulin-related signaling pathways. Tet2, Nsun6, Src, Pi3k, and Akt transcripts exhibited increased m5C enrichment in PCOS ovarian tissues and primary granulosa cells. Concurrently, SRC and PI3K protein expression was increased, whereas AKT protein expression was decreased in the PCOS group. Knockdown of TET2 and NSUN6 was confirmed at the mRNA and protein levels and differentially modulated PI3K/AKT-related protein expression and phosphorylation status, as assessed by PI3K, p-PI3K, AKT, and p-AKT levels. TET2 and NSUN6 knockdown also partially improved PCOS-associated abnormalities in serum FSH, LH, the LH/FSH ratio, testosterone, estradiol, and ovarian morphology. This study reveals a significantly altered mRNA m5C methylation landscape in a DHEA-induced PCOS rat model and primary ovarian granulosa cells. The functional knockdown data suggest that TET2 and NSUN6 may contribute to PCOS-associated ovarian dysfunction through differential regulation or remodeling of PI3K/AKT signaling. However, the opposite changes in the p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT ratios indicate that the pathway is differentially regulated rather than uniformly activated or inhibited. Because the DHEA model primarily mimics hyperandrogenism and MeRIP-qPCR does not provide single-nucleotide resolution, further validation in human samples and high-resolution m5C mapping is required to establish the precise molecular mechanism and clinical relevance of these findings.

title: Tanshinone IIA Inhibits Neuronal Ferroptosis to Alleviate Depressive-Like Behavior in Mice via Regulating Transcriptional Activation of EIF4A3.
abstract: Tanshinone IIA, an active ingredient derived from Salvia miltiorrhiza, is shown to have antidepressant-like activities. We investigated potential molecular mechanism of Tanshinone IIA in the treatment of depression. Chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced mouse model and corticosterone (CORT)-induced HT22 cellular model were established in this study. Depressive-like behavior was assessed by sucrose preference test, forced swim test, and tail suspension test. Hippocampal neuron injury was detected using H&E staining and Nissl staining. CCK-8 was used to detect cell viability. Ferroptosis was analyzed by malondialdehyde assay, intracellular Fe2+ assay, GSH/GSSH ratio, BODIPY-581/591-C11 probe, and transmission electron microscopy. Protein and mRNA expressions were measured by western blot and RT-qPCR. Molecule interactions were validated with chromatin immunoprecipitation, dual-luciferase reporter assay, and RNA immunoprecipitation. Besides, mRNA stability was analyzed using actinomycin D assay. Tanshinone IIA relieved ferroptosis in CORT-injured HT22 cells. Tanshinone IIA alleviated hippocampal neuron ferroptosis and depressive behavior in CUMS-induced mice. Depletion of transcription factor EB (TFEB) counteracted the anti-ferroptosis effect of tanshinone IIA. TFEB could bind to the promoter of eukaryotic initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3), mediating its transcriptional activation. TFEB overexpression inhibited CORT-induced ferroptosis, which was overturned by EIF4A3 knockdown. EIF4A3 depletion reduced the mRNA stability of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), along with decreased BDNF expression and nuclear-related factor 2 (NRF2) nuclear translocation. CORT-induced ferroptosis and decreases of EIF4A3, BDNF, and NRF2 were rescued by tanshinone IIA, which were abolished upon EIF4A3 silencing. Tanshinone IIA improved neuronal ferroptosis and depression in CUMS mice via increasing TFEB. Tanshinone IIA activated TFEB/EIF4A3/BDNF axis to repress neuronal ferroptosis, ameliorating depressive behavior. These findings suggested tanshinone IIA as a promising option for treating depression.

title: Changpu Yujin Decoction Alleviates Tourette Syndrome by Modulating Lipid Metabolism and Microglial Polarization: Involvement of the TREM2/NF-κB Signaling Axis.
abstract: Background: Changpu Yujin Decoction (CPYJD) has been clinically utilized for more than ten years as an effective herbal formula for Tourette syndrome (TS). However, the exact mechanism by which CPYJD treats TS via modulating lipid metabolism and microglia (MG) polarization remains unclear. Methods: A combination of in vivo and in vitro experiments was employed. A total of 72 three-week-old Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were divided into a control group (n = 12) and a modeling group (n = 60). After successful model establishment, the modeled rats were randomly divided into five groups (n = 12 per group): the model group, the tiapride group, and the low-dose, medium-dose, and high-dose Changpu Yujin Decoction (CPYJD-L, CPYJD-M, and CPYJD-H, respectively) groups. All groups were administered the corresponding treatments for 28 consecutive days, and therapeutic efficacy was evaluated by behavioral scoring after the intervention. Neuronal morphology and myelin structure were observed by hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, Nissl staining, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The expression of lipid metabolism- and microglial phenotype-related indicators in each group was detected by immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), biochemical assays, reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), and Western blotting (WB). In addition, lipidomics analysis was performed to identify differential lipid metabolites. For the in vitro experiments, triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) was knocked down in BV2 cells using small interfering RNA (siRNA), and inflammation was induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS). The cells were divided into a control group, an LPS group, a CPYJD-medicated serum group, a TREM2 knockdown group, and a TREM2 knockdown plus CPYJD-medicated serum group. Cell morphology was observed under a microscope, and lipid metabolism- and microglial phenotype-related indicators in each group were detected by immunofluorescence, biochemical assays, RT-qPCR, and WB. Results: Compared with the control group, rats in the model group exhibited significantly increased locomotor activity and stereotyped behaviors, injured striatal neurons with myelin damage, abnormal lipid metabolism and lipid accumulation, an enhanced M1-like pro-inflammatory phenotype with elevated inflammatory cytokine levels, downregulated TREM2 expression, and activation of the nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) signaling pathway. CPYJD reduced stereotyped behaviors and locomotor activity in TS model rats, alleviated neuronal and myelin injury, improved lipid metabolic abnormalities and lipid accumulation, enhanced the M2-like anti-inflammatory phenotype, reduced inflammatory cytokine levels, and upregulated TREM2 expression while inhibiting the activation of the NF-κB signaling pathway. TREM2 knockdown aggravated lipid metabolic abnormalities, lipid accumulation, and the expression of M1-like pro-inflammatory phenotype-related factors in BV2 cells, whereas CPYJD-medicated serum reversed these changes. Conclusions: CPYJD ameliorated pathological injury of striatal neurons, improved lipid metabolic abnormalities and lipid accumulation in MG, promoted a shift in MG from the M1-like pro-inflammatory phenotype toward the M2-like anti-inflammatory phenotype, and reduced inflammatory cytokine levels, thereby alleviating tic symptoms in TS model rats. These effects may be associated with the involvement of the TREM2/NF-κB signaling axis.

title: Distinguishing Plasmablastic/Anaplastic Plasma Cell Neoplasms from Plasmablastic Lymphoma: A Narrative Review and Proposed Integrated Clinicopathologic Framework.
abstract: Plasmablastic/anaplastic plasma cell neoplasms (P/APC-N) and plasmablastic lymphoma (PBL) represent two categories of highly aggressive hematolymphoid malignancies. Their distinction is clinically important because they are classified and treated within different disease frameworks, yet no single morphologic, immunophenotypic, viral, cytogenetic, or molecular finding reliably resolves all cases. The proposed approach begins with the clinical and systemic context, including a pre-existing plasma cell neoplasm, marrow and serum findings, myeloma-defining events, immune status, and disease distribution. Morphologic assessment is followed by a panel evaluating plasma-cell differentiation, conventional B-cell markers, light-chain restriction, proliferative activity, and tumor-cell Epstein-Barr virus-encoded RNA (EBER) by in situ hybridization. Evidence of an established plasma cell neoplasm and a coherent myeloma-associated genomic background favor the relevant plasma cell neoplasm subtype, whereas tumor-cell EBER positivity in a compatible context supports PBL but is not specific. MYC protein overexpression, MYC rearrangement, high proliferative activity, light-chain restriction, and loss of conventional B-cell markers can occur in both categories and should not be used as stand-alone discriminators. When evidence does not converge, reports should state the findings favoring each category, identify unresolved conflicts, and recommend the next diagnostic steps. This framework remains to be validated in independent cohorts.

title: RNA Interference-Mediated Suppression of RAGE.
abstract: The receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE/AGER) is an important mediator of inflammatory signaling and has been implicated in chronic low-grade inflammation associated with aging. Chronic low-grade inflammation ("inflammaging") is a characteristic feature of biological aging, providing a rationale for investigating molecular regulators of inflammatory signaling such as RAGE. This study aimed to develop and validate short hairpin RNA (shRNA) constructs suppressing AGER/RAGE in human cell models. Five shRNA constructs targeting human AGER were designed, cloned into pLSL-puro, and verified by Sanger sequencing. Lentiviral vectors were produced in HEK293T cells and used to establish stable HEK293T, 786-O, and human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC) populations with AGER knockdown. AGER/RAGE expression was assessed by RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and flow cytometry. Silencing efficiency varied with the construct and the cellular model. sh1 produced the strongest suppression of AGER, exceeding 70% in selected models, whereas sh2 was effective in HEK293T and 786-O cells. Reduced RAGE expression was confirmed at the mRNA, protein, and cell-surface levels, identifying sh1 and sh2 as lead candidates. An AGER-focused workflow for lentiviral shRNA construct screening and experimental validation was established, providing a reproducible approach for generating stable cell models with reduced AGER/RAGE expression. Further work is required to confirm isoform specificity, assess off-target effects, and define the functional consequences of RAGE suppression.

title: Proteomic Characterization of Microbiota-Derived Extracellular Vesicle-Enriched Fractions Detected in Red Yeast Rice.
abstract: Fermented foods confer health benefits partially through microbial extracellular vesicles (EVs); however, complex fermented food-derived EVs remain understudied. In this research, we isolated and characterized microbiota-derived EV-enriched fractions (REVs) from 24 red yeast rice (RYR) samples obtained from three Chinese regions. The morphological analysis showed that the EV-enriched fractions exhibited a typical spherical, lipid bilayer structure. Proteomic profiling identified 2376 proteins, including 273 microbiota-derived proteins primarily originating from Monascus, Pectobacterium, and Erwinia species, with 143 proteins showing differential expression among regions. Functional analyses revealed significant enrichment in transport, glycolysis, translation, RNA degradation, and amino acid metabolism. Furthermore, we identified candidate region-associated proteins: rpsK and atpD in the FJ region; ypt-1, ALA1, and MIP11 in the GX region; and trxA, BAB1_1794, pstS, ugpB, tal, and glpK in the ZJ region. As the first comprehensive proteomic characterization of REVs, this study provides a basis for future studies on region-associated protein signatures and the potential application of fermented food-derived EVs in functional foods.

title: Long Non-Coding RNA LINC01614 Promotes Aggressive Phenotypes and Ferroptosis Resistance in Papillary Thyroid Cancer Through a Putative miR-4521/IGF2/PI3K-AKT Signaling Axis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) is the most common endocrine malignancy and is generally associated with favorable clinical outcomes. However, a subset of tumors develops aggressive phenotypes characterized by increased proliferation, migration, therapeutic resistance, and disease progression. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as important regulators of tumor biology, yet the role of Long Intergenic Non-Protein Coding RNA 1614 (LINC01614) in PTC remains poorly understood. This study investigated the functional role of LINC01614 in PTC and its potential involvement in ferroptosis-associated molecular pathways. Methods: RNA sequencing data from a repository of 44 paired PTC and adjacent normal thyroid tissue samples were analyzed to identify differentially expressed lncRNAs. LINC01614 expression was evaluated in thyroid cell lines, and CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) was used to generate stable LINC01614 knockdown K1 cell lines. Cellular proliferation, migration, clonogenicity, intracellular iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation, cytokine secretion, and ferroptosis-associated gene expression were assessed using qRT-PCR, RNA sequencing, Western blotting, cytokine array analysis, iron quantification assays, and BODIPY C11 lipid peroxidation imaging. Results: LINC01614 was significantly overexpressed in PTC tissues and thyroid cancer cell lines. CRISPRi-mediated repression of LINC01614 reduced cellular proliferation, migration, and clonogenic capacity. Mechanistically, LINC01614 knockdown resulted in an 8.8-fold increase in miR-4521 expression and a 23-fold decrease in IGF2 expression, supporting a potential competing endogenous RNA mechanism. Reduced LINC01614 expression was associated with decreased AKT, GPX4, SLC7A11, and SLC3A2 expression, increased IL-6 secretion, a 3.4-fold increase in intracellular ferrous iron accumulation, and a marked increase in lipid peroxidation following erastin treatment, indicating enhanced sensitivity to ferroptosis. Conclusions: These findings identify LINC01614 as a novel regulator of aggressive PTC phenotypes and ferroptosis resistance. The data support a model in which LINC01614 contributes to thyroid cancer progression through modulation of a miR-4521/IGF2/PI3K/AKT signaling axis and downstream anti-ferroptotic pathways. LINC01614 may represent a promising biomarker and potential therapeutic target in papillary thyroid cancer.

title: CDH1 loss remodels gene expression and lineage identity in human mammary epithelial cells.
abstract: Invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) is a common subtype of breast cancer, molecularly defined by genetic loss of CDH1, and subsequent loss of cell adhesion protein E-cadherin, in ~95% of ILC. Though CDH1 loss occurs early in ILC oncogenesis, it is unclear how this facilitates transformation. We modeled early CDH1 loss using "normal" human mammary epithelial cells (HMEC), i.e., finite lifespan cells reflecting early hyperplasia, and targeted E-cadherin signaling using antibodies versus causing genetic CDH1 loss using siRNA or CRISPR/Cas9-knockout. Transcriptome analysis across four HMEC models showed that the mode of E-cadherin targeting is critical for the subsequent phenotype. Antibody-mediated inhibition of cell-cell contacts induced gene signatures of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), consistent with the role of E-cadherin suppression during the EMT process. Conversely, genetic CDH1 loss - as in ILC oncogenesis - repressed EMT signatures, and instead remodeled gene expression toward a luminal epithelial phenotype. RNA-seq, single cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, microscopy, and ATAC-seq analyses support that CDH1 loss induces lineage remodeling to a luminal state, which is mirrored in transcriptomic analysis of clinical ILC precursor lesions. By isolating luminal versus basal cells prior to CDH1 knockout, we found that CDH1 loss led to remodeling of lineage identity in both populations, converging on a new lineage homeostasis with a luminal progenitor-like phenotype. Consistent with the shift to a luminal progenitor phenotype, CDH1 loss enhanced proliferative capacity over the finite lifespan of the HMECs, highlighting a feature of early CDH1 loss that may contribute to clonal advantage during tumor initiation. Moreover, CDH1 loss enhanced anoikis resistance, a defining feature of ILC cells. Our findings support that genetic loss of CDH1 in mammary epithelial cells induces transcriptional and phenotypic changes consistent with lineage identity remodeling toward a luminal progenitor-like state, which may underpin the mechanism by which early CDH1 loss mediates ILC oncogenesis.

title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals archetypal regulatory programs shared across T cell subsets.
abstract: T cells differentiate into functionally distinct subsets in response to pathogens, yet essential immune functions such as self-renewal, expansion, cytokine production, and cytotoxicity are common to multiple subsets and therefore must be programmed via shared regulatory mechanisms. To uncover these "archetypal" epigenomic programs, we integrated a single-cell multiomic (scATAC+RNA-seq) dataset of CD4 and CD8 T cells responding to acute and chronic viral infection with a comprehensive bulk ATAC-seq compendium. Our analysis reveals a modular architecture governing T cell identity, implicating distinct transcription factors in reusing regulatory programs across subsets and lineages. Notably, translationally important progenitor CD8 T cells, critical for sustained immunity and present in both acute and chronic infection, exhibit a composite regulatory state, combining a CD8 exhaustion program with a follicular helper CD4 T cell program. In sum, this resource and generalizable computational framework will aid the mechanistic dissection of adaptive immunity and immunotherapy design.

title: Magnoflorine Ameliorates MASH in Mice Fed a High-Fat and High-Fructose Diet by Promoting AMPK-Mediated Lipophagy and Fatty Acid Oxidation.
abstract: Emerging as a significant clinical burden, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) continues to challenge global healthcare systems due to limited effective interventions. Magnoflorine, a naturally occurring quaternary aporphine alkaloid abundant in dietary botanicals, has demonstrated promising hypolipidemic and anti-inflammatory properties in preliminary investigations. This investigation systematically evaluated both the therapeutic potential and mechanistic pathways underlying the capacity of magnoflorine to ameliorate MASH-associated hepatic pathologies. Male C57BL/6 mice received 12-week high-fat and high-fructose diet (HFFD) induction to establish MASH models, with graded magnoflorine dosing. Through integrated histopathology (H&E/ORO/Masson), transcriptomics, and targeted interventions at both cellular and animal levels, we elucidated the therapeutic mechanisms of magnoflorine. Results showed that magnoflorine effectively alleviated hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis in HFFD-fed mice. Mechanistically, RNA-seq revealed that the 5'-monophosphate AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation was the central pathway mediating the effects of magnoflorine to impede MASH progression. Furthermore, AMPKα activation induced by magnoflorine stimulated hepatic lipophagy in HFFD-fed mice, which further affected lipid β-oxidation and inflammation. The findings were consistent in HepG2 cells incubated with palmitic acid. In vitro, silencing AMPKα reversed the stimulatory effect of magnoflorine on lipophagy in HepG2 cells. In vivo, liver-specific AMPKα silencing in mice blocked the enhancement of hepatic lipophagy and the improvement of MASH caused by magnoflorine. In brief, this study indicates that magnoflorine improves MASH in mice by activating hepatic lipophagy via AMPKα-dependent effects. This discovery provides a novel potential therapeutic alternative for MASH.

title: Comparative Mitogenomics Reveals Mitochondrial Diversity of Haemonchus contortus, a Major Gastrointestinal Parasite of Ruminants.
abstract: Haemonchus contortus is a highly pathogenic hematophagous gastrointestinal nematode and one of the most important constraints to small-ruminant health and productivity worldwide, causing anemia, reduced weight gain, decreased milk production, and substantial economic losses. Understanding its genetic diversity and population structure is essential for improving parasite surveillance and informing sustainable control strategies. In this study, individual H. contortus larvae collected from Pakistani livestock were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, and complete mitochondrial (mt) genomes were assembled and analyzed using comparative mitogenomics, phylogenetic reconstruction, pairwise genetic distance estimation, and haplotype network analyses. Forty-one H. contortus larvae were successfully characterized for their mitochondrial genomes. The first complete mitochondrial genome of Pakistani H. contortus was 14,002 bp in length and comprised 12 protein-coding genes, 22 transfer RNA genes, and two ribosomal RNA genes, with a marked AT content of 78.37%. Mitochondrial genome organization and gene order were highly conserved relative to published H. contortus mitogenomes. Comparative analyses resolved the Pakistani isolates into two well-supported mitochondrial lineages, while maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis clustered all isolates within a robust H. contortus clade clearly distinct from H. placei (bootstrap support, 97-100%). Pairwise genetic distances among Pakistani isolates ranged from 0.00 to 0.05, indicating pronounced nucleotide divergence. Haplotype network analysis identified numerous unique haplotypes together with globally shared haplotypes, supporting substantial mitochondrial diversity. Collectively, these findings provide the first complete mitogenomic resource for H. contortus from Pakistan and advance our understanding of the genetic structure of this economically important veterinary parasite. The generated genomic resource will support molecular epidemiology, population genetic studies, veterinary parasite surveillance, and future investigations of parasite dissemination and anthelmintic resistance in ruminant production systems.

title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.
abstract: As domestic and international travel has expanded, the risk of the cross-border dissemination of infectious pathogens has increased, as clearly evidenced during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aircraft- and airport-based wastewater surveillance can provide timely, aggregate evidence of pathogen circulation among mobile populations and may complement clinical, genomic, and syndromic surveillance at points of entry. The strongest evidence for this approach comes from SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and variant monitoring in aircraft lavatory wastewater, airport terminal wastewater, and airport-associated wastewater systems. However, aviation wastewater signals require cautious interpretation because detectability depends on pathogen shedding dynamics, passenger lavatory use, flight duration, sampling matrix, sample volume, assay sensitivity, sequencing depth, and the availability of epidemiological metadata. This structured narrative review synthesizes current evidence on aircraft and airport wastewater surveillance and examines the scientific determinants that influence surveillance validity and interpretation. Key methodological considerations include sampling design, sample preservation, nucleic acid extraction, molecular detection, sequencing, bioinformatics, inhibition assessment, recovery controls, assay sensitivity, and quality assurance. The review emphasizes that wastewater signals are aggregate and matrix-dependent and should not be interpreted as individual-level diagnosis, direct evidence of transmission, or definitive attribution to a specific flight, route, country, or population. Although SARS-CoV-2 surveillance is comparatively well-documented, multi-pathogen surveillance for enteric viruses, respiratory viruses, vaccine-preventable infections, emerging pathogens, and antimicrobial resistance markers requires pathogen-specific validation and clearer interpretation criteria. Aircraft and airport wastewater surveillance is therefore best viewed as an early-warning and situational-awareness approach whose value depends on converting technical signals into scientifically interpretable evidence.

title: Transcriptome Analysis of Hepatitis C Virus-Infected Hepatoma Cells Following Stringent Removal of Genomic DNA.
abstract: Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) is a positive strand RNA virus that infects hepatocytes and reprograms cellular gene expression, contributing to chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma. HCV replicates slowly and induces limited changes in the cellular transcriptome. Here, we improved analysis of low-abundance transcripts, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), in the context of HCV replication. We stringently removed genomic DNA from total RNA from Huh-7 hepatoma cell lines by a combination of TRIzol, acidic phenol, silica matrix columns and recombinant DNase I. RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) and targeted validation were used to characterize Lnc-ITM2C-1 splice variants and expression of its neighboring gene, G protein-coupled receptor 55 (GPR55), to investigate their potential roles in HCV replication. Challenging our previous findings, under our improved experimental conditions, Lnc-ITM2C-1 and GPR55 were neither involved in a positive regulation circuit with HCV nor induced detectable transcriptome changes. Secondary analysis of RNA-Seq data according to HCV infection status revealed statistically robust HCV-induced expression of 21 host cell genes involved in pathways like stress response (in particular ATF3), lipid metabolism, cytoskeleton organization and growth regulation. In contrast, we found that expression changed for only a limited subset of previously reported HCV-associated lncRNAs (e.g., EGOT). This highlights the necessity of stringent gDNA removal for analysis of low-abundance transcripts like lncRNAs.

title: Effects of Partial Replacement of Palm Oil with Schizochytrium Oil on Rumen Microbiota, Ruminal Volatile Fatty Acid Concentrations, Rumen Epithelial Transcriptome, and Serum Metabolome in Hu Lambs Fed a Medium-Fiber Diet.
abstract: Schizochytrium oil (SO) is rich in docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), but its ruminal effects in sheep remain unclear. Twenty Hu lambs were fed CK or SO diets for 84 d. The CK diet contained 4% palm oil, 31.43% neutral detergent fiber (NDF), and 5.58% ether extract (EE). The SO diet contained 3% palm oil and 1% SO, with similar NDF (31.76%) and EE (5.45%). Blood samples were collected one day before slaughter, before the morning feed replenishment, whereas rumen contents and epithelial tissue were collected after slaughter following a 16-h fast. Rumen microbiota, volatile fatty acids (VFAs), epithelial morphology (n = 10/group), RNA-seq (n = 4/group), and serum metabolomics (n = 5/group) were analyzed. The results showed that the rumen microbial community structure did not differ between the two groups (PERMANOVA, R2 = 0.101, p > 0.05), but SO selectively altered the relative abundance of seven genera (FDR < 0.05), including higher Fibrobacter and lower Methanosphaera. These changes were accompanied by higher acetate, propionate, butyrate, valerate, and total VFA concentrations and a lower acetate/propionate ratio (p < 0.05). Histological analysis showed that rumen papilla length and total epithelial thickness were higher in the SO group than in the CK group (2286.49 vs. 1764.30 μm and 114.52 vs. 80.07 μm, respectively; p < 0.05). Rumen epithelial RNA-seq showed enrichment of pathways related to VFA metabolism, energy metabolism, and fatty acid metabolism in the SO group (FDR < 0.01). Serum metabolomics showed higher levels of DHA and several DHA-containing lipids in the SO group (FDR < 0.05). Overall, partial replacement of palm oil with 1% SO selectively altered selected rumen genera and increased ruminal propionate concentration, accompanied by changes in rumen epithelial morphology and metabolism and increased serum DHA-related lipids. These findings support the potential of SO as a dietary DHA source for Hu lambs and provide evidence for its effects on the rumen and serum DHA-related lipid profile.

title: Integrated Transcriptome-Translatome Analysis Reveals Translational Buffering in the Liver of Chickens Infected with Fowl Adenovirus Serotype 4 Strain GXYL-03, a Strain with Reduced Virulence.
abstract: Fowl adenovirus serotype 4 (FAdV-4) causes hydropericardium-hepatitis syndrome (HHS) and has resulted in severe economic losses to the poultry industry in China since 2015. In this study, we isolated a naturally occurring strain with reduced virulence designated GXYL-03, which caused no gross or histological HHS lesions in 4-week-old specific pathogen-free (SPF) chickens infected at 106 TCID50, whereas clinical signs and partial mortality were observed at higher doses of 107-108 TCID50. After a single immunization with 5 × 104 TCID50 of GXYL-03, all ten immunized SPF chickens survived throughout the 14-day observation following lethal GX2017-005 challenge, whereas all ten challenge-control chickens died. Integrated transcriptome and translatome analyses were performed on the livers of chickens infected with FAdV-4 strains of differing virulence by RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and polysome profiling, with three biological replicates per group. The polysome/non-polysome (P/NP) ratio did not differ significantly among groups (p > 0.05), indicating stable global translation flux. The GXYL-03 group had 2,131 transcriptomic differentially expressed genes (DEGs) but only 71 translatomic DEGs; the GX2017-005 group had 7767 and 148, respectively, indicating that only 3.3% and 1.9% of transcriptional perturbations were transmitted to translation, revealing a pronounced translational buffering effect. Translation efficiency (TE) changes were predominantly suppressive, and downregulated genes accounted for 58.6% and 61.8% of TE changes in the two strains. The functional enrichment of genes whose expression was synchronously upregulated at both levels (TE+RNA+) revealed that GXYL-03 was enriched mainly in protein-coding genes involved in cellular stress, DNA damage repair, vesicle transport, and protein homeostasis (HSPA2, HSPB9, FANCD2, EHD2, and Vault), whereas GX2017-005 was enriched in liver injury-related genes (CD74, ATG2B, FKBP5, ND1, and COX1) that were not differentially expressed in GXYL-03. This study provides insights into the development of FAdV-4 strains with reduced virulence and virus-host interactions.

title: Heat Stress Responses During Grain Filling in Two Korean Wheat Cultivars as Affected by Developmental Stage and Exposure Duration.
abstract: High temperature can impair grain development and storage compound accumulation during wheat grain filling, with responses depending on stress intensity, timing, duration, and cultivar. In this study, Saekeumkang and Hwanggeumal were selected from among major Korean wheat cultivars because they differ in grain quality- and starch-related characteristics, providing a basis for comparing cultivar-specific responses to heat stress during grain filling. Plants were exposed to 25/15, 35/25, and 40/30 °C (day/night) temperature regimes for 5 d beginning at 10 or 20 days after heading (DAH), and changes in grain morphology, endosperm and embryo development, 100-grain weight, protein concentration, and storage-related gene expression were evaluated. High temperature altered grain developmental traits and generally reduced 100-grain weight, while the magnitude of these effects differed between cultivars and treatment stages. Grain protein concentration and the expression of starch- and storage protein-related genes also showed cultivar- and stage-dependent responses. In a separate RNA-seq experiment initiated at 10 DAH, plants were exposed to the temperature treatments for either 5 or 10 d, and transcriptomic analysis revealed that heat intensity and exposure duration affected both the number and functional characteristics of differentially expressed genes, particularly those associated with protein folding and quality control, chromatin-related processes, and carbohydrate metabolism. These results indicate that heat responses during wheat grain filling are jointly influenced by developmental stage, exposure duration, and cultivar-specific molecular regulation.

title: Retrotransposons: A New Frontier in In Vivo Genome Engineering.
abstract: Genome engineering has transformed cell therapy, but clinical implementation remains largely confined to ex vivo workflows followed by adoptive cell transfer. These approaches require costly manufacturing, often rely on viral vectors, and carry risks associated with unwanted genomic alterations. Recent advances in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable genome-editing components to be delivered directly to specific cell populations in vivo, eliminating the need for ex vivo manufacturing. Several RNA-based genome-editing approaches have entered clinical trials. Nevertheless, current in vivo approaches remain largely limited to gene disruption or small sequence modifications. Conventional integration of large payloads generally requires DNA donors, which can be immunogenic, have limited nuclear access, and pose substantial LNP formulation challenges. When expression of therapeutic proteins such as chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) is required, LNP-based approaches predominantly deliver mRNA, leading to transient expression, whereas many applications require durable expression through stable genomic integration. Retrotransposons offer a solution because they have naturally evolved to reverse-transcribe RNA templates directly into chromosomal DNA. Engineered retrotransposon-derived platforms can integrate multi-kilobase payloads from RNA without an exogenous DNA donor. These platforms combine durable expression with RNA-only delivery, but clinical translation requires safe permanent integration, copy-number control, efficient delivery of all required components, and sufficient activity in disease-relevant primary cells. In this review, we describe the classes of non-LTR retrotransposons; examine the design principles underlying their adaptation as genome-editing tools; and compare emerging platforms derived from R2, LINE-1, Vingi, and RTE elements. These systems support integration strategies ranging from naturally evolved insertion profiles, such as site-specific insertion into ribosomal DNA (rDNA) or dispersed genome-wide integration, to fully programmable insertion. Several retrotransposon-based platforms have demonstrated multi-kilobase payload insertion, functional engineering of primary human T cells, and in vivo activity in mouse or non-human primate models, demonstrating their clinical promise. We also discuss key translational challenges. With continued optimization, retrotransposon-based platforms have the potential to bridge the gap between transient RNA delivery and durable gene writing, establishing a versatile foundation for the next generation of in vivo genetic medicines.

title: The UAP2-BRR2b Module Regulates Low-Temperature Hypocotyl Elongation by Modulating Pre-mRNA Splicing in Arabidopsis.
abstract: Plants adapt to low temperatures through transcriptomic reprogramming, yet how the core spliceosome maintains splicing fidelity during cold-regulated development remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the role of the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP-associated protein 2 (AtUAP2) in Arabidopsis using genetic, transcriptomic, and biochemical approaches. Under normal conditions (22 °C), uap2, brr2b, and uap2 brr2b mutants showed no obvious developmental defects. Upon low-temperature treatment, however, uap2 displayed a severe impairment in cold-dependent hypocotyl elongation. RNA-sequencing revealed that UAP2 deficiency induced widespread pre-mRNA mis-splicing under cold stress. Ectopic expression of correctly spliced AtGRP7 and AtLOS2 cDNAs in uap2 partially restored hypocotyl growth under cold conditions, supporting their roles as key downstream effectors. Mechanistically, protein interaction assays demonstrated that UAP2 physically binds to the U5 RNA helicase BRR2b. While brr2b mutants exhibited a hypocotyl growth phenotype similar to uap2, the uap2 brr2b double mutant displayed an enhanced growth defect under low temperatures. Overall, our findings suggest that the UAP2-BRR2b complex operates as a functional module required to sustain spliceosomal efficiency under low temperature, providing insights into the potential connection between core splicing machinery dynamics and cold-induced hypocotyl growth responses in Arabidopsis.

title: Genome-Wide Identification of the TCP Gene Family in Tetraploid Potato and Analysis of Their Potential Roles in Tuber Development.
abstract: Potato tuber formation is a complex developmental process regulated by coordinated interactions among multiple phytohormones and genes.
