TEOSINTE BRANCHED1/CYCLOIDEA/PROLIFERATING CELL FACTOR (TCP) transcription factors play important roles in plant growth, development and responses to environmental stimuli; however, their specific functions in tuber development in tetraploid potato remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed genome-wide identification and systematic characterization of the TCP gene family in tetraploid potato, integrated transcriptome profiling, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), protein-protein interaction prediction and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify candidate genes potentially associated with tuber development. A total of 57 StTCP genes were identified across 29 chromosomes and classified into eight subfamilies. Members within the same subfamily generally shared similar gene structures, conserved motifs and protein domains, whereas their promoter regions contained abundant cis-acting elements associated with light and phytohormone responses, growth and development, and stress responses. Expression profiling revealed distinct StTCP expression patterns under temperature stress and across tuber developmental stages. Eight StTCP genes exhibited pronounced stage-specific expression across the four developmental stages, and their expression trends were broadly supported by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). In particular, StTCP42, StTCP55, and StTCP57 showed significantly higher expression at the stolon hook stage than at the other stages (p < 0.05), whereas StTCP20 was significantly upregulated at the subapical swelling stage (p < 0.05). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) of RNA-seq data from the four developmental stages identified 27 co-expression modules. The turquoise, dark red, pink, and green modules were significantly and positively associated with the stolon hook, subapical swelling, initial tuber formation, and tuber formation stages, respectively; the turquoise module showed the strongest positive correlation with the stolon hook stage (r = 0.997, false discovery rate (FDR) = 2.77 × 10-10). Notably, StTCP42 and StTCP57 were both highly expressed at the stolon hook stage and were assigned to the turquoise module. StTCP42 further exhibited high module membership (kME = 0.930) and gene significance (GS = 0.937, p = 6.79 × 10-6), providing convergent evidence for its association with early tuber development by the transcriptomic, qRT-PCR, and co-expression evidence. This study systematically characterised the TCP gene family in tetraploid potato and identified several candidate genes potentially associated with tuber development, particularly StTCP42 and StTCP57. These findings provide a foundation for future functional studies aimed at elucidating the roles of TCP transcription factors in potato tuber formation and development.

title: Transcriptome Analysis of Linalool-Induced Hypopigmentation in B16 Melanoma Cells.
abstract: Plant-derived phytochemicals exhibit significant pharmacological potential in chronic diseases, including melanoma. Since hyperactive melanogenesis is closely linked to melanoma progression, targeting this pathway with natural bioactive agents represents a major therapeutic strategy. The plant-derived terpene linalool induces cancer-specific oxidative stress in colon cancer cells, as we have previously reported. Here, we characterized the effects of linalool on B16-F10 melanoma cells to establish a transcriptomic baseline of hypopigmentation networks using phenotypic assays and high-throughput RNA-seq profiling. Non-toxic doses of linalool significantly inhibited melanin synthesis, accompanied by a marked reduction in tyrosinase protein abundance. RNA-seq identified 31 significantly upregulated and 48 significantly downregulated genes (p < 0.05), with PCA and cluster analysis demonstrating a distinct transcriptomic profile. Functional GO enrichment revealed candidate regulatory networks involving lysosomal components, the neurofilament cytoskeleton, and cell-cycle checkpoints. While core melanogenesis transcripts (Mitf, Tyr, Dct) showed only minor, non-significant variations, key stress-adaptation and cell-plasticity regulators (Mir210, Dll1) were significantly suppressed. This profile indicates a state of latent molecular vulnerability, mirroring the oxidative responses in colon cancer cells. Taken together, these findings provide a foundational transcriptomic repository of linalool-responsive networks, uncovering critical candidate pathways that modulate melanin production and antioxidant defenses to guide future functional validation and therapeutic exploration of botanical bioactives in melanoma research.

title: Genome-Wide Identification and Stage-Dependent Analysis of Odorant-Binding Protein and Chemosensory Protein Genes in the Summer Fruit Tortrix Moth, Adoxophyes orana (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae).
abstract: The summer tortrix fruit moth, Adoxophyes orana, is a major fruit trees pest in Asia and Europe, which rolls leaves for food and generate silk nets to avoid prey by natural enemies. As a polyphagous species whose host plants cover more than 30 species, it relies on the olfactory system to receive odor molecules for feeding and mating. However, the gene resources of olfactory genes remain limited. In this study, we conducted genome-guided RNA-seq analyses and identified 31 putative OBP genes (24 classical, 4 minus-C and 3 plus-C OBPs, 4 PBPs, and 2 GOBPs) and 21 putative CSP genes. These putative OBPs were located in 8 chromosomes, with 11 in Chr15 and 6 in Chr16. Two GOBPs and four PBPs are adjacently located in Chr16, and 18 out of 21 CSPs are concentrated in Chr16. Phylogenetic analyses showed that all the putative OBPs were classified into five clusters, with all GOBPs and PBPs exclusively in cluster III, and all four minus-C OBPs in cluster IV. Expression analyses indicated that putative AoraOBP7/10 were highly expressed throughout larval stages, putative AoraOBP5/6/8/12/15/21/25 were abundant in first-instar larvae, and 18 of 31 putative OBPs were mainly expressed in adults. In addition to rich AoraOBPs in adult antennae, AoraOBP18/19/20/22 were surprisingly highly expressed in male abdomens, and putative AoraCSPs showed complex expression patterns when combining RNA-seq analyses and RT-qPCR analyses. These results provide a gene resource for future functional studies of OBPs and CSPs, which potentially act as targets for pest management.

title: miR-221/222 Profiles in Small Extracellular Vesicles Derived from Gemcitabine-Sensitive and -Resistant A549 Cancer Stem-like Cell Spheroids: An In Vitro Study.
abstract: Background: Gemcitabine is used in the treatment of human non-small cell lung cancer (hNSCLC), yet acquired resistance can limit therapeutic responses. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) and microRNAs (miRNAs) have been implicated in chemoresistance-associated intercellular signaling. We profiled the miR-221/222 cluster and resistance-associated genes in cancer stem-like cells (CSLCs) and CSLC-derived sEV preparations from gemcitabine-sensitive and -resistant A549 models. Methods: Gemcitabine-resistant A549 cells and matched cancer stem-like cell (CSLC) and gemcitabine-resistant cancer stem-like cell (Gr-CSLC) populations were generated and characterized by flow cytometry, qRT-PCR, and immunofluorescence. sEV preparations derived from CSLC and Gr-CSLC spheroids were characterized for total protein content, EV-associated tetraspanins, and vesicular morphology. PKH26-associated fluorescence following exposure of A549 cells to labeled sEV preparations was also evaluated. The relative levels of sEV-associated miR-221/222 family members and the resistance-associated genes MDR1, ABCG2, and BCL2 were assessed by qRT-PCR. Results: Gr-CSLCs exhibited enhanced spheroid formation and increased MDR1 expression. Gr-CSLC-derived sEV preparations showed higher total protein content than CSLC-derived preparations. Bead-based flow cytometry demonstrated EV-associated CD9 and CD81 expression, while cryo-TEM revealed small, membrane-bound vesicular structures. PKH26-associated intracellular fluorescence was observed in A549 cells following exposure to labeled sEV preparations. Gr-CSLC-derived sEVs showed higher relative levels of miR-221-3p, miR-222-3p, and miR-222-5p than CSLC-derived sEVs, whereas miR-221-5p showed no significant difference. MDR1 and BCL2 also showed higher relative expression in Gr-CSLC-derived sEVs, whereas ABCG2 showed no significant difference. Conclusions: sEV preparations derived from gemcitabine-resistant Gr-CSLCs exhibited distinct miR-221/222 and resistance-associated RNA profiles compared with those derived from gemcitabine-sensitive CSLCs in this in vitro A549 NSCLC model. These molecular differences should be interpreted as associations with the resistant phenotype rather than evidence of functional transfer of chemoresistance. Further functional studies and validation in additional NSCLC and patient-derived models are required to establish their biological, therapeutic, or biomarker relevance.

title: Euonymus alatus-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Show Immunomodulatory Effects in an Inflammatory Thyroid Follicular Cell Model: Insights from Multi-Omics Analysis.
abstract: Objectives: To extract and identify extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from the traditional Chinese herb Euonymus alatus (EA), characterize their molecular profiles using multi-omics analysis, and assess their regulatory effects and potentially associated signaling pathways in an interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-stimulated inflammatory thyroid follicular cell model mimicking key inflammatory features of autoimmune thyroiditis (AIT). Methods: Differential centrifugation combined with density gradient centrifugation was used to purify EA-derived EVs, and the isolates were characterized using a BCA protein assay, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), and Western blotting (WB). Molecular constituents were examined via label-free proteomics and RNA-seq. Meanwhile, Nthy-ori-3-1 cells were exposed to IFN-γ to establish an inflammatory thyroid follicular cell model; these activated cells were subsequently treated with the purified EVs (EV group). The supernatants were collected and the levels of interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and interleukin-18 (IL-18) were determined by ELISA. Comparative transcriptomic and proteomic profiling was employed to identify differentially expressed molecules and related signaling pathways between the model and the EV group. Results: EA-derived EVs were successfully isolated and showed typical EV characteristics. Proteomics identified 3607 proteins enriched in metabolic, immune, and antioxidant processes, while RNA-seq generated 72.16 million clean reads and revealed genes enriched in metabolic and immune pathways. In the IFN-γ-stimulated Nthy-ori-3-1 cells, ELISA results showed that EV treatment significantly reduced the secretion of IL-1β and IL-18 compared to the model group. EV intervention resulted in 138 differential proteins (42 upregulated, 96 downregulated) and 262 differential genes (81 upregulated, 181 downregulated). GO analysis revealed significant enrichment in terms related to inflammatory response, immune response, and regulation of oxidative stress. KEGG pathway analysis demonstrated enrichment in the IL-17, NOD-like receptor, and PPAR signaling pathways, as well as ferroptosis, and Wnt pathway (unique for upregulated genes). Conclusions: EA-derived EVs are rich in molecules that regulate metabolic pathways and immune responses. They may ameliorate inflammation in this inflammatory thyroid follicular cell model, with multi-omics analyses revealing correlative enrichment of multiple signaling pathways. These findings provide preliminary experimental evidence and novel candidate targets for AIT treatment.

title: Periodontal Regeneration Using a Mineralizing Hydrogel Loaded with a Synthetic CEMP1-Derived Peptide.
abstract: Background: Periodontal regeneration requires the coordinated reconstruction of mineralized and non-mineralized tissues. P35 polypeptide derived from Cementum protein-1(CEMP1) has been demonstrated to induce bio-mineralization in vitro, although in vivo applications still need to be further validated. In this study, we developed a novel mineralizing hydrogel system (P35/ACP@PEG Hy) to facilitate periodontal regeneration by encapsulating P35-loaded amorphous calcium phosphate nanoparticles (P35/ACP-NPs) within a four-arm polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogel. Methods: In vitro assays were performed to characterize the physicochemical properties, sustained-release behavior, osteogenic/cementogenic effects of P35/ACP-NPs on hPDLCs, together with the mechanical performance and biocompatibility of the PEG hydrogel. The regenerative capacity of the hydrogel was further assessed in a rat periodontal defect model using micro-CT and histological staining. The regenerative efficacy was evaluated in a rat periodontal defect model via micro-CT and histological staining, while transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) and immune-blotting were further performed to confirm the molecular mechanisms. Results: P35/ACP@PEG exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, featuring an initial burst release followed by a sustained gradual release profile, along with the excellent biocompatibility. In vitro, P35/ACP-NPs markedly promoted osteogenic and cementogenic differentiation of hPDLCs. Correspondingly, the P35/ACP@PEG hydrogel significantly accelerated periodontal tissue regeneration in the rat model with periodontal defect. And RNA-seq analysis and immune-blotting further revealed that these effects are highly linked to activation of the TGF-β/Smad2/3/LOX signaling pathway. Conclusions: P35/ACP@PEG Hy platform can promote periodontal regeneration via activation of TGF-β/Smad2/3/LOX signaling pathway in vivo. Its sustained bioactivity, favorable biocompatibility and robust regenerative efficacy highlight a potential of P35 polypeptide for periodontal tissue repair.

title: Stromal Vascular Cell-Mediated Inflammatory and Remodeling Pathways in Alcohol-Induced Visceral Adipose Tissue Dysfunction: A Pilot Study.
abstract: Chronic alcohol use induces adipocyte lipolysis and production of inflammatory mediators from adipose tissue (AT). Stromal vascular cells (SVCs) are a heterogeneous group of AT cells and contribute to AT inflammation and remodeling in metabolic syndrome. However, the role of SVCs in promoting AT dysfunction upon alcohol exposure remains unclear. Male rats were fed a Lieber-DeCarli diet containing 6.7% (v/v) ethanol (ET) or an isocaloric control diet (CON) for six weeks. Primary rat SVCs were isolated from visceral AT (VAT) of CON and ET rats. RNA sequencing analysis was performed to determine the overall changes in the gene-expression profile. Real-time PCR, Western blotting, and histological analyses were performed to validate the transcriptomics results. Chronic alcohol feeding decreased the adipocyte size and increased the formation of crown-like structures in the rat VAT. RNA-seq analysis revealed that signaling pathways related to cellular response to interleukin 1 (IL1) and collagen-containing extracellular matrix were significantly altered upon ethanol exposure in SVCs. Along these lines, ethanol exposure increased the protein levels of purinergic receptor P2Y2 (P2RY2) and IL1β in the SVCs of rat VAT. Furthermore, ethanol increased collagen deposition in both interstitial and perivascular regions, which was associated with an increase in the level of phosphorylated SMAD2/3 and collagen type VIII alpha 1 chain expression. These findings suggest that chronic ethanol exposure is associated with inflammatory and remodeling-related alterations in VAT and the total VAT-derived SVC fraction. This exploratory pilot study identifies P2RY2-associated inflammatory markers and TGFβ-related remodeling markers as candidates for future mechanistic investigation.

title: Host-Virus Immune Interactions in Andes Virus Infection: Implications for Human-to-Human Transmission, Pathogenesis, and Public Health.
abstract: The Andes virus (ANDV, Orthohantavirus, andesense) is unique among hantaviruses in that it may transfer from person to person and cause severe vascular damage. The evidence on host-virus immunological interactions and their importance in disease progression, transmission, and public health is compiled in this narrative review. ANDV mostly affects pulmonary endothelial cells and does not result in widespread cell loss. Rather, the loss of vascular barrier integrity is caused by vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling, Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) activation, breakdown of vascular endothelial (VE)-cadherin, hypoxia-related pathways, and mediators produced from infected pericytes. Additionally, the virus interferes with early antiviral defenses involving protein kinase R (PKR), TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1)-interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3), mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS), and retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)/melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5). The intensity or outcome of the disease has been associated with increased interleukin-6 (IL-6), altered complement activity, thrombocytopenia, neutralizing-antibody reactions, and specific host genetic variations; nevertheless, significant T-cell activation does not necessarily correspond with viral clearance. Blood and a number of mucosal and secretory samples have been found to contain ANDV ribonucleic acid (RNA), albeit RNA discovery by itself does not prove the presence of an infectious virus. Epidemiological evidence indicates that Secondary transmission is rare and mostly linked to extended close or intimate contact. Genomic sequencing, when paired with epidemiological evidence, can shed light on transmission chains. Recent outbreaks linked to travel further emphasize the significance of worldwide surveillance and coordinated contact tracing. Prospective studies integrating genomic analysis, serial virological sampling, and standardized exposure evaluation are required to more effectively define the infectious phase and transmission patterns.

title: SUGP1 Deficiency Leads to Splicing Dysregulation and Reduced piRNA Abundance in Insects.
abstract: SUGP1 (SURP and G-patch domain containing 1) participates in splice-site recognition through its interaction with SF3B1, and loss of this factor leads to aberrant splicing. While its role in pre-mRNA splicing is well-documented, its impact on small RNA pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we used CRISPR/Cas9-mediated SUGP1 editing in Bombyx mori BmE cell populations and RNAi to systemically knock down SUGP1 in Drosophila melanogaster. SUGP1 loss caused widespread splicing abnormalities in both species and reduced transposon-derived piRNA abundance as shown by small RNA-seq. Notably, the expression and splicing patterns of known piRNA pathway genes remained largely unchanged. Integrating silkworm transcriptomic data with the Flag-SUGP1 Co-IP/MS interactome revealed no direct association with the components of the piRNA biogenesis pathway, but identified a physical interaction with the Y-box protein (YBX), suggesting a potential link connecting splicing surveillance to RNA metabolism and proteostasis. Collectively, these correlative findings suggest that SUGP1 depletion perturbs global RNA processing, and piRNA reduction may represent a secondary outcome associated with cellular stress or dysregulated RNA metabolism within these two tested insect systems. These results suggest a potential indirect link between SUGP1-dependent splicing regulation and piRNA abundance in the tested insect models.

title: Integrated Full-Length Transcriptomics, RNA-Seq and Peptidomics Define an Isoform-Resolved Skin Defense Repertoire in the Chinese Spiny Frog (Quasipaa spinosa).
abstract: Amphibian skin relies on secreted effectors and inducible immune pathways, but short-read RNA sequencing cannot reliably resolve the transcript isoforms and precursor structures underlying this defense system. We generated the first full-length skin transcriptome for the Chinese spiny frog (Quasipaa spinosa) by integrating pooled PacBio Iso-Seq data with six Illumina RNA-seq libraries and six skin peptidomic libraries from control and Proteus mirabilis-challenged frogs. Because Iso-Seq RNA was pooled across conditions, the long-read data were used to define transcript structure rather than condition-specific isoform changes. The reference contained 58,388 transcripts from 34,247 genes, including 32,215 non-reference models, and 5907 of 19,143 reconstructed loci had multiple isoforms. Among 108,147 predicted ORFs, 17,169 carried an N-terminal secretion signal, and 72 secretory and immune-effector ORFs from 46 genes were prioritized. Gene-level RNA-seq identified 72 differentially expressed genes at Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 1; 27 had higher expression in challenged skin and 45 in control skin. No GO term remained significant after correction, whereas three KEGG pathways did. Among these 72 genes, 60 (83.3%) had at least two full-length models, 53 (73.6%) contained at least one complete ORF, and 4 (5.6%) had peptide-sequence support. Reported peptide sequences matched 1029 entries across the full-length catalog, but shared peptide matches were not treated as ORF-specific evidence. Together, these data establish an isoform-resolved skin-defense resource for Q. spinosa and a framework for prioritizing secretory and immune candidates for isoform-specific and functional validation.

title: Effects of Different Formulations of Exogenous Nutrient Bag Waste on Soil Properties and Physiological Activities and Root Transcriptomic Responses of Oat.
abstract: This study used typical chestnut soil from Huangyuan County, Qinghai Province as the experimental soil, and selected three oat varieties, "Baiyan 7", "Qingyan 2", and "Qinghai 444", for mixed sowing. A blank control (CK) and five treatments with different ratios of exogenous nutrient bag waste (PF-R-1 to PF-R-5) were established. Through soil physicochemical analysis, microbial biomass determination, RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), the effects of exogenous nutrient bag waste with different ratios soil nutrient availability, microbial activity and root gene expression in oats were systematically evaluated. The results showed that most treatments enhanced soil organic matter, nitrogen content, and microbial activity. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the comparison between PF-R-3 and PF-R-2 treatments exhibited the highest total number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with enrichment in pathways related to ribosomal protein translation, oxidative phosphorylation energy metabolism, and DNA damage repair. These enrichment patterns suggest potential changes in energy metabolism and protein synthesis, although direct functional validation was not performed. Moreover, DEGs uniquely identified in PF-R-3 were significantly enriched in nitrogen metabolism and secondary metabolite biosynthesis pathways; WGCNA identified the coral2 module as the core regulatory module, with its genes predominantly enriched in functions related to transmembrane transport and plant hormone signal transduction, which were highly consistent with efficient root nutrient acquisition and the maintenance of metabolic homeostasis. Fluorescence staining confirmed the successful colonization of oat root tissues by Morchella mycelium. Taken together, based on the integration of soil nutrient supply stability, root gene expression regulation, and fungal colonization evidence, the PF-R-3 treatment (wheat + corncob + oat) emerged as a promising candidate among the tested formulations under the experimental conditions. However, further field trials incorporating yield and quality data are needed before a definitive recommendation can be made. This study provides a theoretical basis and technical support for the resource utilization of exogenous nutrient bag waste and the green cultivation of oat in alpine regions.

title: High-Dose Gestational Irradiation Disrupts Fetal Mouse Brain Structure and Region-Specific Transcriptomic Profiles.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Prenatal exposure to ionizing radiation can disrupt neurodevelopment, yet the region-specific structural and molecular responses of the developing brain remain incompletely understood. In particular, how gestational irradiation alters transcriptional programs across distinct fetal brain regions and whether these responses differ by sex has not been fully characterized. This study examined the structural and transcriptomic responses in the fetal mouse brain following high-dose gestational irradiation. Methods: Pregnant BALB/c mice were exposed to 1.8 Gy of X-ray irradiation on gestational day (GD) 14.5, and fetal brains were collected on GD 18.5. Results: Using a previously characterized model of radiation-induced fetal growth restriction, H&E-stained sagittal fetal brain sections revealed reduced hippocampal volume and enlargement of the lateral ventricle, while cerebellar volume and optical density were not significantly altered. RNA-seq analysis of the telencephalon, diencephalon, midbrain, and hindbrain revealed region-specific transcriptional dysregulation enriched for genes associated with immune and inflammatory signalling, neurogenesis, gliogenesis, cell migration, and neurotransmitter signalling, with the strongest response observed in the telencephalon and differing DEG profiles between males and females in sex-stratified analyses. Conclusions: These findings indicate that high-dose gestational irradiation is associated with region-specific structural alterations and transcriptional changes in the fetal brain, generating hypotheses regarding the mechanisms of radiation-induced neurodevelopmental disruption.

title: Genome-Wide Characterization of the bZIP Gene Family in Winter Jujube Highlights ZjbZIP7's Association with Late Fruit Development.
abstract: Background: Basic leucine zipper (bZIP) transcription factors function widely in plant development, hormone signaling, and fruit ripening, but the bZIP family and its potential regulatory roles in winter jujube fruit development remain poorly characterized. Methods: a genome-wide analysis was performed using the gapless genome assembly of winter jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill. cv. Dongzao), including phylogenetic, chromosomal distribution, gene duplication, synteny, gene structure, conserved motif, and promoter cis-element analyses. Developmental expression patterns were investigated using RNA-seq and RT-qPCR. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and a yeast one-hybrid assay were further used to examine the co-expression relationships of ZjbZIP7 and its promoter-binding association with ZjACO1. Results: A total of 52 ZjbZIP genes were identified and classified into nine phylogenetic groups. These genes were unevenly distributed across 11 chromosomes, and 11 segmentally duplicated gene pairs were detected. Comparative synteny analysis identified 46 syntenic bZIP gene pairs between winter jujube and the sour jujube (Z. jujuba var. spinosa) and 42 between winter jujube and Arabidopsis thaliana. Promoter analysis identified 53 types of cis-acting elements associated with light, phytohormones, stress responses, and development; notably, abscisic acid-responsive elements were present in 47 of the 52 promoters. RNA-seq analysis across seven fruit developmental stages showed that 18 ZjbZIP genes accumulated preferentially during the late stages, with ZjbZIP7 showing particularly pronounced transcript accumulation during the late developmental stages. RT-qPCR analysis of eight representative genes broadly confirmed their RNA-seq profiles. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified 38 genes tightly co-expressed with ZjbZIP7, including the ethylene biosynthesis gene ZjACO1. A yeast one-hybrid assay further demonstrated that ZjbZIP7 bound to the ZjACO1 promoter in yeast. Conclusions: These findings enhance our understanding of the evolutionary relationships and developmental expression patterns of the ZjbZIP gene family as a whole and provide valuable candidate genes for elucidating fruit-ripening mechanisms that may be useful in improving fruit quality in winter jujube breeding.

title: Mechanisms and Research Progress of LncRNA-Mediated Regulation of Viral Infections.
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), a class of RNA molecules whose transcripts exceed 200 nucleotides in length and typically lack protein-coding capacity, were once widely regarded as "transcriptional noise." However, recent studies have shown that lncRNAs can encode small peptides and play critical roles in biological processes, including gene expression regulation, cell differentiation, and immune response. Viral infections, as a common disease, can reshape the transcriptome of host cells, in which the differential expression of lncRNAs is a core link in host-virus interactions. This review aims to deeply analyze the multidimensional regulatory mechanisms of lncRNAs in the host antiviral innate immune response. It elaborates in detail on how lncRNAs construct the host antiviral defense by regulating pattern recognition receptor (PRR) signaling pathways, the production and signal transduction of interferons (IFNs), as well as the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs). Additionally, we conducted an in-depth analysis of the complex functions of lncRNAs in regulating programmed cell death (PCD), including key processes such as pyroptosis, autophagy, and apoptosis, and integrated specific research cases in infections caused by multiple significant viruses, including influenza A virus (IAV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). We aim to provide novel strategies for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of viral diseases.

title: Heterogeneously Expressed GadAB Identified by Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Mediates Antibiotic Tolerance Under Acid Stress.
abstract: Bacterial population heterogeneity serves as the intrinsic basis for persister formation. Single-cell RNA sequencing is a powerful tool for investigating such heterogeneity. In this study, we analyzed single-cell transcriptomic data, previously generated via RiboD-PETRI-seq, from exponential-phase Escherichia coli MG1655 populations. We identified subpopulations with heterogeneous expression of gadA and gadB. Dual-fluorescent reporter strains were subsequently utilized to verify the heterogeneous protein abundance of GadA and GadB across the bacterial community. The expression levels of these two proteins were positively correlated within individual cells. We further observed that the naturally occurring GadA/GadB-low subpopulation exhibited a higher persister ratio than the GadA/GadB-high subpopulation under acid stress, and a similar phenotype was recapitulated in the ΔgadAB mutant. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses collectively demonstrated that the gadAB double mutant exhibits a dormant-like state upon acid exposure. This study confirms heterogeneous gadA and gadB expression within bacterial populations. The GadA/GadB-low subpopulation exhibits enhanced antibiotic tolerance under acid stress. This work offers theoretical insights into the acid and antibiotic tolerance mechanisms of enteric pathogens in the acidic gastrointestinal niche.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Distinct Pathogenic Subtypes in Hepatocyte- and Cholangiocyte-Directed Autoimmune Liver Injury.
abstract: Autoimmune liver diseases (AILDs) involve a group of distinct disorders, but the differences in pathogenic subpopulations that drive hepatocyte or bile duct injury remain unclear. This study characterizes immune niche heterogeneity across AILD subtypes using single-cell RNA sequencing and verifies findings with animal models. We identified distinct immune cell states and functions by analyzing the heterogeneity of T cell and macrophage subsets and the impact of non-immune cell-derived signals on macrophage identity. This allowed us to characterize two distinct immunopathogenic ecotypes between hepatitis and cholestatic phenotypes. Mechanistic analysis predicted the Bmp-Acvrl1/Eng-Fosb signaling axis as a critical transcriptional regulator driving the repair phenotype of macrophages. Notably, Eng (endoglin) emerged as a regulatory receptor controlling macrophage phenotypic transition, especially during the recovery phase of cholestatic disease. Collectively, this study provides a comprehensive atlas of immune cell niches across AILDs, offering new mechanistic insights into disease heterogeneity and identifying macrophage maturation as a promising target for stratified therapeutic intervention in cholestatic disease.

title: Shenqi Granules Ameliorate Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury by Regulating Glucocerebrosidase and Uridine Metabolism in Microglia.
abstract: Objective: Shenqi Granules is a traditional Chinese medicine formula derived from the classic prescription Shenqi Formula (SQF), composed of Astragali Radix (Huangqi) and Codonopsis Radix (Dangshen). SQF shows neuroprotection in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods: The rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) was established using the suture method to evaluate the neuroprotective effect of SQF. Blood-absorbed components were identified via UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, and potential targets and pathways were predicted through network pharmacology. Non-targeted metabolomics of serum and feces was performed using UHPLC-Orbitrap MS, and core metabolic pathways were selected based on regulation magnitude (RM). Gut microbiota structure was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, with associations between microbiota and metabolites assessed via the Mantel test and redundancy analysis (RDA). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to screen core Hub genes for ischemic stroke (IS). Based on single-cell RNA data, a uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional signature score (Uridine_Score) was constructed, and cell type-specific coupling between glucocerebrosidase (GBA) and this transcriptional signature was analyzed. Microglial temporal trajectory analysis was conducted using Monocle3. Molecular docking between core components and GBA was verified by AutoDock, and GBA mRNA expression was confirmed by RT-qPCR. Results: High-dose SQF reduced infarct volume and neuronal damage and improved behavior. A total of 28 absorbed components and 31 shared IS targets were identified. Metabolomics revealed nucleotide metabolism as a core pathway common to both serum and fecal samples. SQF restored gut-blood uridine balance (serum uridine 0.41× Sham → 0.85× post-SQF), reduced fecal dTMP and hypoxanthine. 16S rRNA sequencing demonstrated that the overall correlation between microbial community structure and nucleotide metabolites was statistically significant (Mantel r = 0.307-0.321, p < 0.01). WGCNA highlighted GBA, MMP9, and PYGL. Single-cell analysis showed a microglia-specific uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional signature post-stroke, with GBA most correlated with this signature (ρ = 0.377). Pseudotime revealed microglial state transitions (Homeostatic → Acute_Reactive → DAM), with positive GBA-uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional coupling in the Homeostatic and DAM states. Riboflavin showed the strongest GBA binding (-9.83 kcal/mol), and SQF upregulated GBA mRNA in the penumbra (p < 0.0001). Conclusions: SQF reprograms nucleotide metabolism via the gut-blood axis and enhances microglial GBA-uridine transport/metabolism-associated transcriptional coupling.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Distinct Molecular and Immune Microenvironment Features of Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome-Associated Lobular Endocervical Glandular Hyperplasia and Gastric-Type Endocervical Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Background: Gastric-type endocervical adenocarcinoma (GAS) is an aggressive, human papillomavirus-independent cervical adenocarcinoma, whereas lobular endocervical glandular hyperplasia (LEGH) is considered a potential precursor. Molecular and immune microenvironment differences between Peutz-Jeghers syndrome-associated LEGH (PJS-LEGH) and GAS (PJS-GAS) remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to characterize these differences through integrated transcriptomic analysis. Methods: Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on tissues from 7 PJS-LEGH and 8 PJS-GAS cases. Differential expression and functional enrichment analyses were integrated with weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), molecular interaction network analysis, and machine learning. Immune-related transcriptional patterns were assessed using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) and xCell, with CD45/CD4 multiplex immunofluorescence for preliminary tissue-level assessment. Results: We identified 1794 differentially expressed genes, including 976 upregulated and 818 downregulated genes in PJS-GAS. Functional and network analyses highlighted differences involving ciliary biology, epithelial differentiation, chemokine signaling, and immune regulation. ssGSEA revealed higher scores for selected T-cell, dendritic-cell, monocyte, and myeloid-derived suppressor cell signatures in PJS-GAS. xCell provided complementary evidence of higher scores for selected immune-cell populations, together with activation- and inhibition-associated transcriptional signatures. Integrated analyses converged on PTPRC, encoding the pan-leukocyte marker CD45, as a prominent leukocyte-associated feature of PJS-GAS. Multiplex immunofluorescence showed higher CD45+ and CD4+ cell densities in the sampled PJS-GAS tissues. Conclusions: This study provides the first transcriptomic comparison of PJS-LEGH and PJS-GAS and identifies distinct molecular features and increased immune-cell-associated transcriptional signatures with coexisting activation- and inhibition-associated expression patterns in PJS-GAS.

title: Ferritin Heavy Chain 1 Sustains Steroid Hormone Synthesis in Sheep Granulosa Cells by Suppressing Erastin-Induced Ferroptosis.
abstract: Litter size is a critical trait determining the economic efficiency of sheep production. Ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1), a key iron-storage protein, plays an important role in regulating cellular susceptibility to ferroptosis. Based on our previous observation that ferroptosis-related pathways differ between ovaries from single-lamb and multi-lamb Hu ewes, this study investigated the role of FTH1 in regulating ferroptosis and granulosa cell (GC) function in sheep. FTH1 expression was examined in ovarian tissues and GCs from Hu sheep with different reproductive phenotypes and follicular developmental stages using RT-qPCR. An erastin-induced ferroptosis model was established in sheep GCs, and FTH1 function was evaluated through overexpression and interference experiments. Ferroptosis-related indicators, including ROS, C11-BODIPY 581/591, Fe2+, malondialdehyde (MDA), reduced glutathione (GSH), ferroptosis-associated genes, and GPX4 protein expression, were analyzed. Steroidogenic function was assessed by measuring the expression of STAR, CYP11A1, HSD17B1, and 3β-HSD, as well as estradiol (E2) and progesterone (P4) secretion. RNA sequencing was performed to identify transcriptional changes associated with FTH1 overexpression in erastin-treated GCs. FTH1 expression was higher in ovaries from multiparous sheep and healthy follicles. FTH1 overexpression alleviated erastin-induced ferroptosis by enhancing GPX4 expression and reducing Fe2+ accumulation, ROS production, and lipid peroxidation, whereas FTH1 knockdown aggravated ferroptosis damage. Furthermore, FTH1 maintained steroidogenic function by promoting STAR expression and preserving E2 and P4 synthesis under ferroptosis stress. Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) partially rescued GC viability and steroidogenic capacity, and attenuated erastin-induced apoptosis. Under erastin treatment, transcriptome analysis identified 297 differentially expressed mRNAs and 92 lncRNAs between FTH1-overexpressing GCs and the corresponding vector control. These differentially expressed transcripts represent candidate regulatory relationships that require further functional validation. Enrichment analysis highlighted cytokine signaling and ROS-related pathways, suggesting potential processes associated with the effects of FTH1 under these conditions. Collectively, these findings support that FTH1 protects sheep GCs against ferroptosis-induced injury and supports steroidogenic function, providing new insights into the role of iron homeostasis in follicular development.

title: Integrative Analysis of Whole Exome Sequencing and Gene Expression to Uncover Genetic Mechanisms in Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic immune-mediated disorder of the gastrointestinal tract. This study aimed to nominate candidate genes and pathways for IBD by integrating exome sequencing and gene expression data. Methods: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed on 10 patients with Crohn's disease (CD). Differential expression was analyzed with GEO2R in an independent RNA-seq dataset (GSE193677; 2490 biopsies from 1162 subjects). Immune-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified with ImmPort, hub genes by protein-protein interaction analysis, and enriched pathways with Enrichr. Missense variants were modeled with AlphaFold 3. Results: WES identified 484 genes with rare coding variants in all 10 patients, and 732 genes were differentially expressed in CD or ulcerative colitis, 234 of them immune-related. Network, pathway, and database filtering prioritized ATM, CSF1R, FN1, and IL11, which together carry eight rare missense variants, with in silico predictions ranging from tolerated to deleterious. Enriched pathways included cytokine and interleukin signaling, and structural modeling predicted conformational changes. Conclusions: ATM, CSF1R, FN1, and IL11 are candidate genes in immune-related pathways in IBD. Because the genomic and expression data came from different cohorts, these genes need replication and experimental validation.

title: Multi-Platform Transcriptomic Classification of LUAD Driver Mutation Subtypes via Heterogeneous Ensemble Learning.
abstract: Background: Accurate identification of EGFR-mutant, KRAS-mutant, and triple-negative (TN) LUAD driver mutation subtypes is essential for guiding targeted therapy, yet standard molecular testing is invasive and not always feasible. Gene expression-based machine learning offers an alternative that avoids additional invasive sampling; however, existing models are largely restricted to binary classification and lack cross-platform generalizability. Methods: We developed a multi-cohort, ComBat-harmonized pipeline integrating SHAP-driven feature selection and a Bayesian-optimized heterogeneous ensemble of five learners, extended with NSGA-II Pareto-optimal weight optimization under leak-free cross-validation. External validation used an independent RNA-seq cohort with reference-batch harmonization and threshold calibration. Results: ParetoVoting achieved the best internal performance (F1-macro = 0.736, AUROC = 0.877), statistically indistinguishable from SoftVoting (F1-macro = 0.735; Cliff's δ=-0.12), which was carried forward for external validation. On TCGA-LUAD (n=508), SoftVoting attained F1-macro = 0.700 and AUROC = 0.850, though this reflects an out-of-range KRAS threshold (representative value ∼0.66-0.68). Ablation analysis showed components contributed unequally within internal cross-validation, with ComBat's critical role instead emerging during cross-platform external generalization. SHAP analysis identified biologically coherent signatures consistent with known LUAD oncogenic signaling. Conclusions: This framework provides a reproducible, cross-platform approach to three-class driver mutation subtyping from transcriptomic data, offering benchmarks for this underexplored task and potential clinical utility where tissue-based profiling is infeasible.

title: Plasma and Serum Metagenomic Sequencing of Microbial Cell-Free Nucleic Acids for Suspected Central Nervous System Infection: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Untargeted metagenomic sequencing of microbial cell-free DNA or RNA in plasma or serum offers pathogen detection without lumbar puncture or biopsy, but its value in suspected central nervous system (CNS) infection is uncertain. We reviewed diagnostic yield, agreement with CNS-site testing, clinical impact, and failure modes. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched with seven documented strings (inception to 2 September 2026), supplemented by citation and web searching. Eligible reports were primary human studies of untargeted plasma or serum metagenomic sequencing with a separable result in patients with suspected or confirmed infectious CNS syndromes. Selection, extraction, and design-specific risk-of-bias appraisal followed PRISMA 2020 and were performed independently by two authors with disagreements resolved by discussion; the search was restricted to PubMed/MEDLINE and no protocol was registered. Synthesis was narrative because designs and reference standards were incompatible. Results: Of 190 reports assessed, 69 studies were included (18 denominator-based cohorts, 8 small series, 43 case reports; 51 from the United States). Positive CNS-specific clinical impact in commercial assay cohorts ranged from 0 of 24 adult to 5 of 24 pediatric meningoencephalitis tests. Among 51 case-level reports, the plasma or serum result was concordant with CNS-site testing in 28, positive when CNS-site testing was negative in 5, unconfirmed in 12, and negative or missed the pathogen in 6. All five plasma-only detections came from single case reports, which contributed to no yield or agreement denominator; excluding the four abstract-level case reports moved no proportion by more than 1.3 percentage points. RNA viruses, low-burden focal mould disease, and chromosomally integrated HHV-6 were recurrent sources of false-negative or misleading results. Conclusions: Plasma or serum metagenomic sequencing is a useful adjunct in selected difficult CNS infections, particularly disseminated, fungal, amoebic, or fastidious bacterial disease, but it does not replace CNS-site diagnostics.

title: Transcriptomic Identification and Functional Assessment of Candidate Host Factors Affecting Akabane Virus Replication.
abstract: Akabane virus (AKAV) causes abortion, stillbirth, and congenital malformations in ruminants, yet the transcriptional response of Madin-Darby bovine kidney (MDBK) cells and the roles of infection-responsive host genes in AKAV replication remain incompletely characterized. We profiled AKAV-infected and time-matched mock-infected MDBK cells by RNA sequencing at 12 and 24 h post-infection (hpi). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were examined using Gene Ontology functional classification and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway enrichment analysis, six DEGs were evaluated by RT-qPCR, and OAS2 and ZBP1 were assessed by overexpression in BHK-21 cells. We identified 119 DEGs at 12 hpi (82 upregulated and 37 downregulated) and 149 at 24 hpi (85 upregulated and 64 downregulated). The DEG sets were associated with antiviral defense, interferon responses, pattern recognition receptor signaling, DNA replication, cell cycle regulation, chromosome organization, and metabolism. RT-qPCR measurements were consistent with the RNA-seq trends. OAS2 and ZBP1 transcripts were significantly upregulated at 12 hpi, while ZBP1 transcript levels remained significantly elevated at 24 hpi. Overexpression of either gene was associated with reductions in AKAV Gc protein abundance, viral RNA levels, and infectious titers. These results define transcriptional changes in AKAV-infected MDBK cells and nominate OAS2 and ZBP1 as candidate host factors for further investigation, while their endogenous roles in bovine cells remain to be established.

title: Multi-Omics Integration Reveals Molecular Signatures Associated with Pork Quality Differences Between Liaodan Black and Xinjin Pigs.
abstract: This exploratory study investigated meat quality differences and associated molecular characteristics between Liaodan Black (LDM) and Xinjin (XJM) pigs, two local breeds from Northeast China, using meat quality, fatty acid, and total amino acid measurements together with transcriptomic, proteomic, and untargeted metabolomic analyses of the longissimus thoracis et lumborum muscle (n = 3 per breed for all analyses). XJM pigs had higher intramuscular fat content and lower shear force, whereas LDM pigs had higher cooking yield. After correction for multiple testing, XJM pigs had higher oleic acid content. Total amino acid analysis showed higher serine, arginine, proline, methionine, and phenylalanine contents in XJM pigs, whereas isoleucine and leucine contents were higher in LDM pigs. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses identified 5678 differentially expressed genes and 533 differentially abundant proteins, respectively, while untargeted metabolomic analysis revealed 622 differential metabolites based on putative annotations. These molecular differences were mainly associated with cytoskeletal organization, oxidative phosphorylation, protein turnover, amino acid metabolism, and central carbon metabolism. Transcriptome-proteome integration identified 258 shared differential features, of which 139 showed concordant changes at the mRNA and protein levels. Integrated analysis identified nine candidate molecules. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, exploratory correlation analysis showed that GOT1 and GLO1 protein abundances were negatively associated with shear force and cooking yield, whereas ESD protein abundance was positively associated with IMF content. qPCR analysis of selected DEGs showed good agreement with RNA-seq results (r = 0.883, p < 0.001). Overall, the differences observed between the sampled LDM and XJM groups were mainly associated with lipid deposition, muscle structure-related processes, and energy metabolism.

title: TPD54 Downregulates ERK Signaling in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Cells.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Epidermal growth factor receptor is frequently overexpressed in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and is associated with poor prognosis. We previously demonstrated that members of the tumor protein D (TPD) 52 family regulate the malignant behavior of OSCC cells and that epidermal growth factor (EGF) induces TPD52 expression. In this study, we investigated the relationship between the TPD52 family and EGF signaling, focusing on TPD54. Methods: SAS OSCC cells were treated with EGF and gefitinib, and the expression of TPD52 family members (TPD52, TPD53, and TPD54) was analyzed using reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and Western blotting. Nascent RNA and RNA degradation assays were conducted to investigate the mechanisms regulating TPD52 family expression. TPD54-overexpressing and TPD54-knockdown cells were used to evaluate EGF signaling, cell cycle progression, proliferation, apoptosis, autophagy, migration, and invasion. Results: EGF stimulation increased the mRNA expression of all TPD52 family members. Nascent RNA analysis revealed increased transcription, whereas RNA degradation assays indicated reduced mRNA stability. TPD54 overexpression attenuated EGF-induced ERK phosphorylation and suppressed EGF-induced cell cycle progression. However, under the present experimental conditions, TPD54 had little effect on cell proliferation, apoptosis, autophagy, migration, or invasion. Conclusions: TPD54 is an EGF-responsive protein that suppresses EGF-induced ERK activation and attenuates cell cycle progression in OSCC cells. Although TPD54 exerted minimal effects on cell proliferation, apoptosis, autophagy, invasion, or migration under the tested conditions, these findings suggest that TPD54 functions as a negative regulator of EGF signaling and provide insight into its molecular role in OSCC.

title: UCHL1 Promotes Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition Through E-Cadherin and N-Cadherin Switch in Endometrial Cancer.
abstract: Objective: Endometrial cancer (EC) is one of the most common cancers in women, and its incidence is increasing worldwide. The prognosis of recurrent and advanced cancer remains poor because treatment options are limited. Ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase-L1 (UCHL1) is associated with the progression of several cancers including EC. In this study, we analyzed the function of UCHL1 in EC progression. Methods: UCHL1 expression in the serum of patients with EC was measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Changes in cell migration and invasion were analyzed in UCHL1-overexpressing or UCHL1-knockdown cells (UCHL1-OE/UCHL1-KD) using wound-healing and transwell assays. Messenger RNA expression of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related genes in each cell was detected using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). UCHL1 and EMT marker proteins were detected with Western blotting and an immunofluorescence assay (IFA). Results: Serum UCHL1 expression was significantly elevated in patients with metastases. Wound-healing assays and transwell assays showed that UCHL1 could promote cell migration and invasion. These effects were suppressed by UCHL1 knockdown and inhibition. UCHL1 overexpression modulated the expressions of EMT-related molecules in EC cells at the mRNA and protein levels. Furthermore, IFA analysis showed that changes in EMT-related molecules were consistent with lesions of UCHL1 expression. Conclusions: This study revealed that UCHL1 could contribute to promoting cell migration and invasion. These results may be associated with EMT regulation in EC cells.

title: Interferon-Associated Inflammatory Remodeling and Oxidative Metabolic Repression Define the Skeletal Muscle Transcriptomic Landscape of δ-Sarcoglycan Deficiency.
abstract: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy R6, formerly LGMD2F, is caused by mutations in the δ-sarcoglycan (Sgcd) gene and is characterized by progressive skeletal muscle degeneration. Although loss of δ-SG protein compromises sarcolemma stability, how δ-sarcoglycan deficiency reshapes inflammatory and metabolic gene programs across distinct skeletal muscles remains incompletely defined. Here, we profiled soleus and extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles from wild-type and Sgcd-/- mice treated with vehicle or (-)-epicatechin, a dietary flavanol with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, using bulk RNA sequencing, pathway analysis, immune-cell deconvolution, and RT-qPCR validation. δ-sarcoglycan deficiency produced broad transcriptional remodeling while preserving baseline muscle-type identity. Across soleus and EDL, the dystrophic transcriptome was marked by interferon-associated inflammatory remodeling together with repression of oxidative and mitochondrial metabolic programs. Within this shared disease state, soleus displayed a stronger induced inflammatory component, including innate-sensing and macrophage-linked features. Computational deconvolution, which estimates immune-cell proportions from bulk transcriptomes (quanTIseq and mMCP-counter), supported genotype-dependent shifts in immune-cell signatures, with concordant monocyte/macrophage signals. Finally, (-)-epicatechin produced context-dependent transcriptional effects and attenuated a defined interferon/innate-sensing module in dystrophic soleus, as supported by RNA-seq and RT-qPCR. Together, these findings establish inflammatory remodeling with a prominent interferon component and oxidative metabolic repression as central transcriptional features of δ-sarcoglycan-deficient skeletal muscle, while revealing an amplified innate-sensing and immune-enriched module in dystrophic soleus that remains transcriptionally responsive to (-)-epicatechin treatment.

title: Paired Transcriptomic Profiling Identifies Shared Liver Metastasis-Associated Molecular Features in Colorectal Cancer.
abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CCLM) is closely associated with poor patient prognosis, yet patient-specific molecular heterogeneity complicates the identification of recurrent molecular changes during metastasis. To address this, we performed RNA sequencing on paired primary tumors and liver metastases synchronously resected from six patients and analyzed gene expression changes using a paired design that accounted for interpatient variability. This analysis identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and metastasis-associated pathways through functional enrichment analysis and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). The reproducibility of these changes was further assessed across multiple independent publicly available transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Selected candidate genes were additionally evaluated in a metastasis-selected colorectal cancer cell model, in which several genes showed expression changes consistent with the transcriptomic findings. Together, these results indicate that recurrent molecular changes accompany CCLM despite substantial interpatient heterogeneity and provide a strategy for identifying metastasis-associated molecular features and potential therapeutic targets.

title: Multi-Tissue Transcriptomic Profiles of Tarim and Tianshan Red Deer Under Common Conditions.
abstract: We profiled 132 RNA-sequencing libraries representing 11 tissues from six Tarim and six Tianshan adult male red deer maintained under common feeding and management. Tissue identity dominated expression structure among 16,308 expressed genes. Across three differential-expression model specifications, 1253 robust group-associated gene-tissue pairs were identified, involving 1184 genes and concentrated in rumen and rectum. Directional enrichment returned 77 terms meeting both within-set and study-wide false-discovery thresholds. Tianshan-group rumen genes were enriched for cytoskeletal, adhesion, ion-transport and circadian annotations, whereas Tarim-group reticulum genes were enriched for cell-surface and immune-signaling annotations. Cross-tissue recurrence was uncommon and identified a small set of annotated genes and provisional loci for follow-up. Complementary whole-genome principal component analysis (PCA) separated the recorded groups across two genotype-depth filters; weighted Weir-Cockerham FST was 0.341 and 0.325. These results describe tissue-resolved expression patterns and genetic structure in the sampled cohort. Functional, taxonomic and population-wide interpretations require independent validation.

title: The Proliferation-Invasion Dichotomy: Transcriptomic Signatures of lncRNA and Ubiquitin-Proteasome Networks in Hypermutated Endometrial Cancer.
abstract: Endometrial cancer incidence is markedly rising globally, posing an urgent need to elucidate the molecular mechanisms driving disease characterization and progression. Endometrial cancer evolution is driven by canonical Wnt and p53 pathway alterations, yet the mechanisms orchestrating the transition from localized proliferation to stromal invasion, the proliferation-invasion dichotomy, remain poorly understood. While long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are emerging as critical correlates of divergent tumor phenotypes, their coordination with the broader ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), specifically E3 ligase and deubiquitinase (DUB) networks, during endometrial cancer progression is largely unexplored. Whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue from a clinical cohort of 38 patients, comprising 34 primary endometrial carcinomas across distinct molecular subtypes (MSI, POLE, p53abn, and NSMP) and four pre-cancerous endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia (EIN) lesions. To stringently control for baseline patient-specific confounding, differential gene expression and principal component analyses were executed using a strict, intra-patient, matched-pair design (Tumor vs. Adjacent Normal). A principal component analysis of the batch-corrected transcriptome revealed a profound divergence between tumor and paired adjacent normal phenotypes. This spatial divergence was heavily characterized by lncRNA signatures (including SOCS2-AS1) strongly associated with extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Concurrently, we identified a critical, malignancy-specific transcriptomic dysregulation across the broader UPS network. Within this altered transcriptional landscape, the ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase (UCHL) family emerged as a highly significant node. UCHL5 displayed robust, global upregulation across the pan-cancer cohort compared with matched controls (log2FC = 0.83, padj < 0.001). Strikingly, UCHL3 exhibited global upregulation (log2FC = 1.23, padj = 0.002) that was highly concentrated within the microsatellite instability (MSI) and polymerase epsilon (POLE) hypermutated subtypes, highlighting a potential compensatory transcriptomic response to the predicted cellular stress inherent to high mutational burdens. In an exploratory subset of pre-cancerous EIN lesions (n = 4), neither the invasive lncRNA networks nor profound UPS/UCHL dysregulation were observed, suggesting a preliminary trend that requires validation in larger precursor cohorts. Our paired transcriptomic mapping reveals that endometrial cancer progression is characterized by divergent transcriptomic programs: specific lncRNA networks are tightly coupled to the invasive remodeling of the ECM, while concurrent dysregulation of broad UPS networks reflects the altered proteostasis associated with this phenotypic shift. The pronounced upregulation of critical UPS nodes, such as UCHL3 in MSI/POLE tumors, highlights a landscape of novel, enzymatically targetable vulnerabilities in hypermutated endometrial cancers.

title: Deciphering Vascular Smooth Muscle Cell Phenotype Switching via Integrated Single-Cell Transcriptomics and Machine Learning: CX3CR1 and COL1A1 as Novel Diagnostic Biomarkers for Atherosclerosis.
abstract: Background: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the arterial wall in which immune-cell accumulation and vascular stromal remodeling jointly shape plaque progression and stability. Because bulk-tissue transcriptomes combine signals from multiple cell types, the cellular origin of candidate expression markers must be resolved before they can be interpreted as vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC)-intrinsic features. Methods: We integrated the GSE309462 human carotid-plaque single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset with the bulk arterial-tissue datasets GSE100927 and GSE57691. Intersection-derived genes were prioritized using LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE. Discriminatory direction was standardized for receiver operating characteristic analysis, the five consensus genes were evaluated in the independent plaque-stage dataset GSE28829, and their cellular origins were audited across 99,027 cells from 12 donors. Results: Forty-nine genes were shared between the SMC-cluster-associated gene set and the bulk arterial-tissue differential-expression results. Five genes (MPEG1, CX3CR1, SERPINA3, LMCD1, and COL1A1) were selected by all three machine-learning procedures. In the training data, direction-standardized AUCs ranged from 0.859 to 0.922. In GSE28829, MPEG1, CX3CR1, and COL1A1 showed higher expression in advanced plaques and AUCs of 0.904, 0.827, and 0.928, respectively; LMCD1 was higher in early plaques (AUC 0.870), whereas SERPINA3 showed limited discrimination (AUC 0.442). Single-cell localization showed that MPEG1 and CX3CR1 were predominantly expressed in macrophages, whereas LMCD1 and COL1A1 were enriched in VSMCs and other vascular stromal cells. Conclusion: The expression signature captures compartmentally distinct processes, particularly myeloid-cell infiltration and extracellular-matrix remodeling. These genes should therefore be interpreted as plaque-associated tissue markers and mechanistic candidates rather than validated non-invasive diagnostic biomarkers or definitive VSMC-lineage markers.

title: Follistatin-like Protein 1 Contributes to Acute Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury by Enhancing Neuroinflammation Through the Modulation of Interferon Regulatory Factor 5-Mediated Macrophage Activation.
abstract: Background and Purpose: Follistatin-like protein 1 (Fstl1) is a secreted glycoprotein with context-dependent inflammatory activity. We investigated whether Fstl1 is a reproducible feature of traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) and whether it regulates macrophage activation through interferon regulatory factor 5 (IRF5). Methods: A target-blind analysis integrated four public SCI bulk transcriptomic cohorts with single-cell and spatial datasets. Findings were tested in wild-type and Fstl1+/- mice after SCI using spinal cord RNA sequencing, molecular and histological assays, behavioral testing, and bone marrow-derived macrophages with IRF5 gain- and loss-of-function. Adult-induced Postn-CreER-mediated Fstl1 deletion was evaluated in fibroblast-macrophage non-contact co-cultures. Results: The public-data screen reduced 440 cross-cohort candidates to four non-structural extracellular genes, including Fstl1. Fstl1 was consistently upregulated across SCI cohorts, correlated with myeloid signatures, and was predominantly associated with non-myeloid cell sources in single-cell data. Experimental SCI increased spinal Fstl1 and inflammatory cytokines, whereas partial Fstl1 depletion reduced tissue damage and improved locomotor recovery. Fibroblast Fstl1 deletion reduced macrophage iNOS, Il6, and Tnf and increased Arg-1 and Il10 in co-culture. Spinal cord RNA sequencing showed broad remodeling of immune and tissue-related programs after Fstl1 depletion. Computational perturbation and experimental validation identified IRF5 as a downstream mediator. Recombinant Fstl1 increased IRF5, iNOS, and CD80 while reducing Arg-1 and CD163; IRF5 silencing reversed these changes. Conclusions: Fstl1 is a reproducible SCI-associated extracellular candidate that supports IRF5-dependent inflammatory macrophage activation. Targeting the Fstl1-IRF5 axis may help limit secondary neuroinflammation after SCI.

title: Integrative Molecular Profiling and Single-Cell Characterization of LHFPL5 Reveal Cancer-Specific Regulatory Features in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma and Lung Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Background and Objectives: LHFPL5 encodes a four-pass transmembrane protein essential for cochlear mechanotransduction, but its molecular behavior in cancer remains poorly defined. We characterized the genomic, epigenetic, transcriptomic, immune, and cellular context of LHFPL5 in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (KIRC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), along with its associations with clinical outcomes. Materials and Methods: Retrospective analyses integrated TCGA RNA sequencing, clinical, DNA methylation, copy number, tumor purity, and immune deconvolution data. Transcriptome-wide associations and Hallmark enrichment defined LHFPL5-associated programs. Continuous-expression Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) per standard-deviation increase, adjusted for age, sex, and pathological stage. GEO cohorts assessed external reproducibility, matched TCGA expression pipelines assessed processing sensitivity, and three non-TCGA single-cell datasets examined cellular localization. Results: LHFPL5 showed distinct molecular contexts in KIRC and LUAD. In KIRC, higher expression remained associated with poorer overall survival after clinical adjustment (528 patients; 174 deaths; HR = 1.36, 95% CI 1.21-1.53; p = 2.42 × 10-7), while subtype and immune fractions showed limited statistical overlap with the association. In LUAD, expression covaried with copy-number state and showed a weak inverse relationship with first-exon methylation. Proliferation-related transcriptional programs were associated with survival, although enrichment support depended on the multiple-testing procedure. The primary STAR-derived LUAD analysis was null (485 patients; 177 deaths; HR = 1.02, 95% CI 0.89-1.18; p = 0.770), and survival inference varied with RNA processing. External adjusted replication was inconclusive. Single-cell detection was sparse in KIRC and one LUAD dataset; another LUAD cohort showed more frequent epithelial detection without resolved malignant-cell identity. Conclusions: LHFPL5 exhibits cancer-specific molecular architecture. LUAD showed copy-number, methylation, and proliferation-related associations, whereas KIRC showed a distinct molecular context with an independent survival signal. These findings support context-dependent LHFPL5 regulation and prioritize genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptional mechanisms for functional investigation.

title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Network Pharmacology Analyses Reveal Potential Mechanisms of Codonopsis pilosula in Mountain Sickness.
abstract: Mountain sickness comprises a spectrum of high-altitude disorders associated with hypobaric hypoxia, including acute mountain sickness (AMS) and high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). Although Codonopsis pilosula has been widely used in traditional medicine for conditions related to hypoxia, its molecular basis in mountain sickness remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, single-cell RNA sequencing, and molecular docking to explore potential molecular associations between Codonopsis pilosula-related candidate targets and mountain sickness. We identified a set of Codonopsis pilosula-associated candidate targets enriched in biological processes related to hypoxia response, oxidative stress, inflammation, and vascular regulation. Integrated transcriptomic analyses across high-altitude exposure, AMS, and HAPE revealed convergent alterations in immune-related and oxygen transport-associated programs. Machine-learning analysis further provided internal computational prioritization of candidate genes associated with high-altitude exposure, with recurrent selection across complementary algorithms within the analyzed paired cohort. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis provided additional cellular context for these candidates, revealing distinct expression patterns across peripheral blood and lung cell populations. Molecular docking further identified potential interactions between selected Codonopsis pilosula compounds and candidate proteins, with MMP9, CA2, and BCL2 showing comparatively favorable predicted interactions. Together, these findings provide an exploratory framework for evaluating potential associations between Codonopsis pilosula-associated candidate targets and transcriptional and cellular responses to high-altitude hypoxia, and identify candidate molecular pathways and targets for further experimental investigation.

title: A Biomimetic In Vitro Model of the Pro-Inflammatory Microenvironment Recapitulates Type I/II Interferon Signaling and Refractory Acute Monocytic Leukemia.
abstract: Preclinical drug development suffers from a persistent translational gap, as conventional animal models fail to reproduce the human immune response, contributing to high attrition rates of drug candidates in clinical trials. To address this, we previously established an in vitro high-density culture (HDC) model of acute monocytic leukemia (AML) cells that recapitulates an aseptic pro-inflammatory microenvironment using acute monocytic leukemia (AMoL) THP-1 cells. In the present study, using RNA-seq, quantitative RT-PCR, flow cytometry, Western blotting, and multiplex cytokine analysis, we characterized how this biomimetic microenvironment shapes Type I and II interferon signaling in THP-1 cells that acquire resistance to apoptosis under HDC conditions. The model revealed predominant activation of the Type II interferon pathway, marked by elevated interferon-gamma expression, STAT1 activation, and increased production of interferon-stimulated chemokines. Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified key interferon-induced hub genes and regulatory transcription factors driving this response. Notably, the interferon-stimulated gene profile generated by this in vitro platform, including the Interferon-Related DNA Damage Resistance Signature, closely resembled gene expression patterns observed in clinical samples from patients with refractory AMoL, supporting the relevance of the HDC biomimetic system as a research model of inflammatory adaptation in leukemia cells and associated resistance. These findings support further investigation of the HDC biomimetic system as a research model of inflammatory adaptation in leukemia cells and associated resistance.

title: Transcriptomic Convergence Reveals Tumour-Specific Stromal Remodelling in Immune-Enriched Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
abstract: Although immune activation can occur in both papillary thyroid carcinoma (TC) and nodular goitre (NG), the transcriptional programmes distinguishing malignant from non-malignant immune-rich thyroid tissue remain poorly understood. In this pilot study, bulk RNA sequencing of 19 specimens (10 TC, 9 NG) allowed classification into four tumour microenvironment (TME) subgroups. Immune deconvolution showed that TC Immune-Enriched tumours were characterised by cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) enrichment rather than predominant lymphocytic infiltration. Differential expression analysis identified only nine genes distinguishing TC Immune-Enriched from NG Immune-High tissue, suggesting transcriptomic similarity between malignant and benign immune-activated states in this small cohort. To identify tumour-associated stromal programmes, we identified genes shared between immune-enriched versus immune-depleted comparisons in papillary TC and nodular goitre. This yielded a 441-gene candidate tumour-associated stromal programme enriched for collagen-containing extracellular matrix organisation and TGFβ-associated ECM-remodelling pathways, supported by WGCNA and protein-protein interaction analyses. In 456 TCGA-THCA carcinomas, stromal enrichment correlated inversely with thyroid differentiation and was highest in BRAF-like tumours and the tall-cell histological variant. These findings suggest that transcriptomic convergence largely reflects shared inflammatory programmes, whereas stromal remodelling identifies a candidate tumour-associated stromal programme.

title: Meta-Analysis of ALS Post-Mortem Cerebral Cortex Transcriptome Studies Identifies Robust Shifts in Gene Expression Despite Significant Between-Study Heterogeneity.
abstract: Background: ALS is characterized by motor neuron failure with potential neurocognitive comorbidity. Cortical neurons, and their support cells, exhibit pathologic features, some of which have been identified in post-mortem transcriptome studies of the cortex from ALS patients and control subjects. These studies, however, have utilized varying technologies with few attempts to reconcile findings. Methods: This study used meta-analysis to evaluate differential gene expression (ALS vs. control) from 16 prior transcriptome studies utilizing multiple technologies (microarray, bulk RNA-seq or snRNA-seq). Normalization with GC content correction was used to mitigate downstream biases impacting differential expression. Results: Approximately one-third of protein-coding genes (5930 of 16,579) exhibited significant between-study effect size heterogeneity (FDR < 0.05), which was frequently associated with variation in average post-mortem interval. Nonetheless, we identified 269 and 273 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with relatively consistent increased or decreased expression in the ALS cortex, respectively (FDR < 0.05 with SMD ≥ 0.20 or SMD ≤ -0.20). ALS-increased DEGs were associated with transcription (RNA polymerase), cell signaling (TGF-beta, PI3K), interneurons, microglia, endothelial cells, and deep laminar layers (L5, L6). ALS-decreased DEGs were associated with transcription (RNA polymerase), glial cells (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes) and the L1 layer. There was significant overlap between DEGs from the ALS cortex and those previously identified from ALS spinal cord and blood. Conclusions: These findings highlight signaling pathways, cell types and cortical layers associated with robust changes in ALS cortex gene expression. Our results illustrate the importance of meta-analysis as a tool for understanding between-study heterogeneity and identifying repeatable findings across technologies.

title: Tissue Factor Expression Is Associated with Distinct Pattern of Immune-Cell Infiltration in the Ovarian Tumor Microenvironment.
abstract: Tissue factor (TF) has been implicated in tumor progression and immune regulation, but its cellular sources and relationship with immune infiltration in ovarian cancer remain incompletely defined. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE232314), analyses of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) ovarian cancer cohort, and multiplex immunofluorescence in an independent 25-case tissue microarray (TMA). Single-cell analysis showed that TF expression was concentrated in tumor epithelial cells and a discrete endothelial subpopulation, with minimal expression in immune and other stromal compartments. In the TCGA cohort, TF expression was not significantly associated with tumor stage, grade, disease-free survival, or overall survival. In TF-stratified analyses, however, high CD8+ T cell infiltration was associated with improved survival in the low-TF expression subgroup (HR = 0.60) but with worse survival in the high-TF subgroup (HR = 1.72); high M1 macrophage infiltration was associated with improved survival only in the low-TF subgroup. TF expression correlated negatively with estimated CD8+ T cell, memory B cell, and M1 macrophage infiltration and positively with naïve B cell infiltration. In the TMA cohort, high-TF tumors showed significantly lower CD56+ NK-cell and CD68+ macrophage infiltration and a lower CD68/CD163 ratio. Together, these findings show cross-sectional associations between TF expression and reduced measured abundance of several antitumor immune populations and a stratum-dependent association between CD8+ T cell infiltration and survival. These associations were not fully concordant between the transcriptomic (TCGA) and protein-level (TMA) cohorts and require prospective, formally tested validation. TF warrants further investigation as a candidate immune-context biomarker in ovarian cancer.

title: NINJ1 Defines a Hyperinflammatory Monocyte State Associated with Severe COVID-19.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is characterized by dysregulated immune activation and excessive inflammation; however, the specific immune cell states that drive disease progression remain incompletely understood. Methods: Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells with clinical validation to investigate the role of Ninjurin-1 (NINJ1) in COVID-19-associated immune dysregulation. Results: Single-cell profiling revealed that NINJ1 expression was largely confined to monocytes and defined as a distinct NINJ1+ inflammatory monocyte state in patients with COVID-19.
