Compared with NINJ1- monocytes, NINJ1+ monocytes exhibited enhanced inflammatory transcriptional programs, altered regulon activity, and increased cell-cell communication capacity, suggesting their potential role as a highly activated immune state involved in inflammatory amplification. Further ligand-receptor interaction analysis demonstrated that NINJ1+ monocytes functioned as key communication hubs within the COVID-19 immune landscape, coordinating extensive interactions with other immune populations. In an independent cohort of 99 COVID-19 patients and 51 healthy controls, serum NINJ1 levels were significantly elevated in infected individuals and were further increased in non-survivors. Circulating NINJ1 levels correlated with inflammatory and immune dysregulation indicators, including C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, prothrombin time, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and lymphocyte depletion. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated that serum NINJ1 exhibited significant predictive value for in-hospital mortality. Conclusions: Collectively, our findings identify NINJ1+ inflammatory monocytes as an activated immune state associated with the transition from protective innate defense to pathological inflammation, providing new insights into COVID-19 immunopathogenesis and highlighting NINJ1 as a promising biomarker candidate for risk stratification and therapeutic exploration.

title: Large-scale integrated single-cell analysis reveals molecular subtypes and microenvironmental remodeling in cutaneous T cell lymphoma
abstract: Cutaneous T cell lymphoma (CTCL) comprises a clinically and molecularly heterogeneous group of skin-homing non-Hodgkin lymphomas for which robust biomarkers remain limited. Prior single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies have provided important insights into CTCL biology, but many of these prior studies have been limited by small sample sizes and focused on niche questions of interest. Additionally, many studies have suffered from pseudoreplication, resulting in inflated test statistics and reduced external validity. Here, we assembled and integrated scRNA-seq data spanning 244 unique samples and 132 patients across CTCL, healthy control (HC), and benign inflammatory dermatoses (BID) conditions, generating the most diverse atlas of CTCL to date. Following identification of malignant cell populations and heterogeneous, within-sample gene expression alterations, we applied pseudobulk aggregation and robust linear mixed-effects modeling to nominate recurrent changes across this highly heterogeneous patient cohort. Interrogation of the skin microenvironment identified significant compositional and cell type-specific expression changes in CTCL lesions as compared to control lesions and across clinical stages of disease. Finally, we used unbiased clustering to identify stable, molecularly defined subtypes of disease that were predictive of outcome in an independent dataset. Together, this study provides a rigorous analysis of the most diverse scRNA-seq dataset of CTCL ever compiled, nominating specific alterations in cell type composition and gene expression across malignant cell and microenvironmental populations with significant clinical implications.

title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug perturbation prediction to delineate the molecular determinants of CTC emergence and persistence. Results: Primary tumors from CTC+ patients exhibited distinct transcriptomic profiles characterized by the upregulation of genes involved in PI3K-Akt signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and chromatin regulation (e.g., HDAC1, JUN, KLK10), alongside the downregulation of immune activation pathways, including complement, B-cell receptor (BCR), and T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Multi-gene survival models derived from upregulated (KLK10, MEOX2, IRS4, RND2) and downregulated (ALDH3A1, PPP2R2B, IGF1R) hub genes significantly stratified patient outcomes (HR = 1.74-2.44, p < 0.01). In contrast, primary tumors from CTC- patients displayed early systemic transcriptional alterations relative to healthy controls, with 1700+ DEGs linked to MAPK/ERK and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways, suggesting pre-metastatic immune reprogramming even before CTC detection. Drug repurposing analysis identified Trichostatin A, BX-795, and Alvocidib as candidate compounds capable of reversing the CTC+ transcriptional signature. Conclusions: Rather than supporting a strictly binary view of CTC status, our findings are consistent with a transcriptional continuum of distinct yet partially overlapping primary-tumor transcriptional states associated with CTC- and CTC+ status, highlighting a molecular shift from immune suppression to epigenetic adaptation that facilitates hematogenous dissemination. The identified multi-gene prognostic panels and small-molecule candidates provide a foundation for CTC-targeted therapeutic strategies and early detection biomarkers in breast cancer.

title: SCO2, LYN, and FGR as Mitochondria-Associated Immune-Inflammatory Candidate Signatures Across PMOS and MCI Datasets.
abstract: Background: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), previously known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a prevalent endocrine disorder increasingly associated with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Mitochondrial dysfunction and immune dysregulation may underlie this association; however, shared molecular features between these conditions remain systematically uninvestigated. Methods: We used PMOS (granulosa cell, n = 16) and MCI (peripheral blood, n = 243) to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) intersecting mitochondrial-related genes (MRGs), supported by enrichment and prioritized by machine-learning with cross-validation. Boxplots in PMOS and MCI confirmed directionality. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) identified cell types and communication. In vitro experiments assessed SCO2, LYN, and FGR in cell lines. Results: We identified 16 mitochondrial-related genes shared by PMOS and MCI datasets. Enrichment implicated NF-κB and TNF signaling in PMOS/MCI immunometabolic features. SCO2, LYN, and FGR were upregulated across datasets, although LYN was discordant in granulosa comparison. Single-cell sequencing identified five subtypes. Pseudotime showed SCO2 and LYN upregulation in early/late stages, whereas FGR was undetectable. Secondary annotation identified plasmacytoid dendritic cells, classical monocytes, and pro-B cells; pro-B cells predominated in controls (47.5%) and classical monocytes in disease (40.5%). In vitro validation showed mRNA/protein upregulation of SCO2, LYN, and FGR in PMOS/MCI models versus control. Conclusions: This study identified SCO2, LYN, and FGR as mitochondria-associated immune-inflammatory signatures in PMOS and MCI datasets. Differential expression, feature-ranking models, pathway enrichment, transcriptional deconvolution, single-cell contextualization, and cell assessment support were utilized. Without PMOS-MCI cohorts and functional perturbation experiments, findings remain hypothesis-generating, unvalidated biomarkers or causal mechanisms.

title: Transcriptomic Profiling of PBMCs via Bulk RNA-Sequencing in Posner-Schlossman Syndrome Reveals Immune Dysregulation and Altered Viral Response.
abstract: To explore systemic immune transcriptional signatures in Posner-Schlossman syndrome (PSS) across acute and intermittent phases. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from acute-phase PSS patients (APSS; n = 4), intermittent-phase PSS patients (IPSS; n = 3), and healthy controls (n = 3). Two patients were sampled in both phases; within-subject correlation was not modeled in differential-expression analyses. Differential expression was assessed using DESeq2, pathways were examined using the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes, and immune-cell-associated marker expression was compared using CAMERA gene set testing with linear model contrasts. Plasma IFITM2, ISG15, and SOCS1 were measured by ELISA in an independent cohort of 51 APSS patients and 69 healthy controls. Interferon-responsive and antiviral genes, including IFITM2, ISG15, and SOCS1, were downregulated in APSS. Plasma protein levels showed concordant decreases in the independent cohort. Genes encoding ubiquitin-proteasome components (SKP1, RBX1, PSMF1, PSMB2, PSMB3, and PSMD13) and cytokines associated with antigen presentation and adaptive immunity were downregulated, whereas cytokine genes linked to macrophage activity and innate immunity were upregulated. Post hoc comparisons showed reduced CD8+ T-cell-associated and increased macrophage-associated marker expression in APSS compared with both IPSS and controls. IPSS immune transcriptional profiles generally approached those of controls, consistent with reduced disease activity, although residual differences in macrophage-associated expression remained. These exploratory findings suggest altered systemic innate and adaptive immune regulation in PSS, with an increased monocyte/macrophage-associated transcriptional signature during acute attacks. They do not establish immune-cell proportions or cytomegalovirus-mediated mechanisms and cannot directly represent local anterior chamber pathology.

title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Machine Learning Unveil Plakophilin 1 as a Robust Diagnostic Biomarker for Thymoma.
abstract: Background: Thymoma (THYM) is a rare epithelial tumor originating in the anterior mediastinum. Due to the lack of specific clinical manifestations and reliable molecular biomarkers, its diagnosis and treatment are often delayed until advanced stages. Although multi-omics technologies have provided new strategies for biomarker discovery, systematic integrative studies specifically focused on thymoma remain limited. Objectives: This study aimed to identify and validate potential diagnostic biomarkers for thymoma through the integration of multi-omics data and machine learning approaches. Methods: We integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and epigenomic datasets and applied machine learning algorithms to screen for core candidate genes. The cell-type-specific expression patterns of the identified candidates were further evaluated using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and their potential molecular functions were predicted via in silico perturbation analysis. In addition, immunohistochemistry (IHC) was performed to validate the differential expression of the candidate biomarker at the protein level. Results: Six core candidate genes-interferon regulatory factor 6 (IRF6), thyroid hormone receptor interactor 6 (TRIP6), plakophilin 1 (PKP1), cadherin 1 (CDH1), pre-B-cell leukemia transcription factor 1 (PBX1), and keratin 1 (KRT1)-were identified through machine learning. Among these, PKP1 demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance in both the training set (area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, AUC: 0.83; sensitivity: 0.80; specificity: 0.875) and the validation set (AUC: 0.94; sensitivity: 0.93; specificity: 1.000). Single-cell RNA sequencing confirmed a significantly enriched expression pattern of PKP1 in thymoma tumor cells. In silico perturbation analysis suggested that PKP1 may be involved in cell adhesion and tumor progression through regulation of the extracellular matrix (ECM)-integrin-cytoskeleton axis. Immunohistochemistry further validated the significantly elevated protein expression level of PKP1 in thymoma tissues. Conclusions: This study identifies PKP1 as a potential diagnostic biomarker for thymoma with high diagnostic performance and tumor cell-enriched expression, providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying thymoma progression and its potential clinical applications.

title: Integrative Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies Candidate Endothelial Activation Signatures in Atopic Dermatitis.
abstract: Background: Endothelial activation is a recognized histological feature of atopic dermatitis (AD), but its transcriptional programs remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We reanalyzed public single-cell RNA-seq data from the skin of five patients with AD and four healthy donors using AD-associated gene set scoring, CellChat, endothelial hdWGCNA and pseudotime ordering, and examined candidate genes with eight machine learning classifiers and SHAP in public bulk transcriptomes of lesional and non-lesional AD skin. Results: Inferred intercellular interactions were more numerous in AD (1348 vs. 1111), with COLLAGEN, CD99 and MIF showing the largest gains in communication strength. Differences in AD-associated gene set scores between AD and healthy endothelial cells were small and inconsistent between scoring approaches. Among seven endothelial modules, Endo7, an NF-κB-responsive immediate-early module containing SELE, ICAM1, IRF1 and NFKBIA, overlapped most strongly with the AD gene set (10 genes; approximately 30-fold enrichment). AD endothelial cells were concentrated at intermediate pseudotime positions (Cohen's d = 0.334). In bulk skin, classifiers based on 14 LASSO-selected genes separated lesional from non-lesional AD skin in a small test set (AUC 0.70-0.98; likely optimistic estimates, as feature selection preceded the training-test split and paired samples from the same patients may span both partitions), with SELE, TOP2A and IRF1 ranked highest by SHAP. Conclusions: This hypothesis-generating analysis identifies AD-associated endothelial activation signatures and candidate genes that require confirmation in independent, clinically characterized cohorts and experimental studies.

title: Oxidative stress-driven cellular heterogeneity in Knee Osteoarthritis: scRNA-seq pinpoints SPP1 and CYBA for diagnostic development.
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage degeneration, synovial inflammation, and subchondral bone remodeling. Oxidative stress plays a critical role in KOA pathogenesis. This study aimed to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with machine learning to uncover potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for KOA. ScRNA-seq data from KOA cartilage tissues were obtained from the GEO database to characterize cellular heterogeneity and identify disease-associated chondrocyte subsets. CellChat was used to analyze intercellular communication, and Monocle2 was applied to reconstruct cell differentiation trajectories. Oxidative stress activity at the single-cell level was evaluated using AUCell, while high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) was performed to identify oxidative stress-related gene modules. Candidate genes were screened using Venn analysis and further refined by LASSO regression, SVM-RFE, and XGBoost combined with SHAP analysis. Diagnostic performance was assessed, and biological relevance was explored through immune infiltration and pathway analyses. Experimental validation was conducted using qRT-PCR and western blot assays in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. InfC and ProFC were detected specifically in OA cartilage and exhibited high oxidative stress activity. InfC was enriched in inflammatory and immune-related pathways, whereas ProFC was associated with cell cycle regulation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Integrated hdWGCNA and machine-learning analyses consistently identified CYBA and SPP1 as candidate genes. The two-gene model achieved bootstrap-corrected AUCs of 0.937 and 0.825 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. qRT-PCR and western blot analyses further showed increased CYBA and SPP1 expression in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. Conclusion InfC and ProFC may represent OA-associated chondrocyte states characterized by enhanced oxidative stress, while CYBA and SPP1 may serve as candidate diagnostic biomarkers. Given the small cohort sizes and preliminary in vitro validation, these findings require confirmation in larger independent cohorts and functional studies.

title: Integrated Multi-Omics Characterization of WASHC2C Reveals Cancer-Specific Molecular, Clinical, Immune, and Cellular Associations.
abstract: WASHC2C encodes a WASH-complex scaffold implicated in actin remodeling, endosomal organization, and intracellular trafficking, yet its cancer-specific molecular and clinical relevance remains insufficiently defined, particularly in the context of the closely related paralogue WASHC2A. An integrated pan-cancer multi-omics analysis was performed incorporating transcriptomic and protein-level evidence, clinicopathological and survival associations, genomic and epigenetic alterations, pathway activity, gene-set enrichment, immune features, immunotherapy-related observations, and single-cell functional states. Primary RNA analyses extracted both paralogues from the same GDC STAR files across eight cancer types, while covariate-adjusted Cox models evaluated LUAD, BLCA, and LIHC. A locked 50-gene co-expression signature was additionally assessed in independent GEO cohort, GSE31210. The harmonized expression analysis comprised 4365 primary tumors and 429 normal specimens and revealed pronounced lineage-specific variation together with strong WASHC2A-WASHC2C co-expression. Although HNSC showed platform-dependent directional differences between STAR and GSCA, the integrated analyses identified LIHC as the clearest prognostic context: higher WASHC2C expression was associated with poorer overall survival in the primary adjusted model (340 patients; 115 deaths; HR = 1.61 per unit log2[TPM + 1], 95% CI 1.18-2.21; FDR = 0.035), although the magnitude of association varied with model specification. Favorable unadjusted observations in LUAD and BLCA were not retained after covariate adjustment, and primary BLCA OS/DSS models were non-estimable. Across cancers, copy-number variation showed a consistent positive relationship with transcript abundance, whereas pathway, immune, methylation, and single-cell associations demonstrated marked tumor-context specificity. In GSE31210, 48 measurable genes from the locked signature were associated with favorable survival in 204 patients, supporting the relevance of the broader co-expression program, although neither WASHC2C nor WASHC2A contributed directly to that score. Collectively, this study establishes a rigorous multi-omic framework for WASHC2C, highlights its lineage-dependent molecular and prognostic relevance, and prioritizes specific cancer contexts-particularly LIHC-for mechanistic and translational investigation. These findings provide a strong foundation for future paralogue-resolved functional studies and independent clinical validation.

title: Cross-Cancer Characterization of CAMK2A Reveals Its Favorable Prognostic Association and Neuronal Signature Enrichment in Glioma.
abstract: Background: Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II alpha (CAMK2A) is a neuron-enriched kinase that plays essential roles in synaptic signaling and neuronal differentiation. However, its clinical significance and biological relevance in glioma remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to systematically characterize CAMK2A across human cancers and investigate its prognostic significance and association with neuronal differentiation programs in glioma. Methods: An integrated multi-omics analysis was performed using pan-cancer transcriptomic, proteomic, genomic, DNA methylation, bulk RNA-sequencing, and single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets from TCGA, CPTAC, GTEx, CGGA, and other public resources. CAMK2A expression patterns, clinical associations, prognostic value, molecular characteristics, pathway activities, and cellular localization were systematically evaluated. Multiplex immunofluorescence staining of human glioma specimens was further performed to validate the protein-level expression patterns of CaMKII and the neuronal marker MAP2. Results:CAMK2A exhibited lineage-specific dysregulation across human cancers and was progressively downregulated during glioma progression. Higher CAMK2A expression was consistently associated with prolonged overall survival across multiple independent glioma cohorts and remained an independent favorable prognostic factor after adjustment for established clinicopathological and molecular variables. Functional enrichment analyses linked CAMK2A to neuronal differentiation, synaptic organization, calcium signaling, and neurotransmission-related pathways. Gliomas with high CAMK2A expression exhibited lower scores for several malignancy-associated pathways and enrichment of neuronal transcriptional signatures; these tissue-level associations do not distinguish tumor-intrinsic programs from normal neuronal admixture. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses further revealed preferential enrichment of CAMK2A in neuronal populations. Consistently, multiplex immunofluorescence demonstrated a coordinated reduction in CaMKII and MAP2 protein expression with glioma progression. Conclusions:CAMK2A represents a neuron-associated biomarker linked to preserved neuronal differentiation programs and favorable clinical outcomes in glioma. These findings support its potential value as a prognostic biomarker and provide further insight into the relationship between neuronal differentiation programs and glioma progression.

title: Identification of CLOCK and MARK2 as Candidate Blood-Based Biomarkers in Type 2 Diabetes: An Integrated Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Study.
abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is often accompanied by nervous system complications. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying T2DM remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify candidate blood-based biomarkers associated with T2DM by screening a neural-related gene set through integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood. The present analysis focused on the systemic expression patterns of the selected genes in peripheral blood as indicators of T2DM-associated immunometabolic dysregulation, rather than on neurological involvement. The neural-related gene set was used only as a predefined screening starting point. Methods: We employed a three-tier validation framework comprising (1) a training cohort (GSE15932, 8 T2DM patients vs. 8 controls) for biomarker discovery using differential expression analysis and machine learning (XGBoost, random forest, and PPI network topology); (2) an independent validation cohort (GSE184050, 50 T2DM patients vs. 65 controls) for cross-dataset diagnostic performance assessment (ROC analysis); and (3) an experimental validation cohort (5 T2DM patients vs. 5 controls) for independent clinical confirmation by RT-qPCR. Additionally, single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE268210) was used to investigate cell type-specific expression and immune regulatory networks. Results: By combining multiple screening methods and cross-dataset validation, we identified CLOCK and MARK2 as key candidate genes from the neural-related gene set. CLOCK and MARK2 showed high discriminatory performance in the discovery cohort, whereas their AUCs were 0.613 and 0.653, respectively, in the validation cohort, indicating limited standalone discriminatory ability. Both genes are highly expressed in peripheral blood monocytes and are associated with MIF-(CD74+CXCR4)-mediated cell communication, TNFA-NFκB inflammatory signaling, and activation of oxidative phosphorylation pathways. Finally, RT-qPCR in clinical samples confirmed that both genes were indeed upregulated (p < 0.05). Conclusions:CLOCK and MARK2 were identified as candidate T2DM-associated blood-based biomarkers with reproducible expression differences across datasets. Their discriminatory performance was more modest in the independent validation cohort, indicating limited standalone diagnostic utility. Single-cell and computational analyses further suggested potential immunometabolic relevance. Because neurological phenotyping, cognitive assessment, and direct measures of nervous system involvement were not available in this study, any relationship between these genes and the neurological manifestations of T2DM remains speculative and hypothesis-generating, and requires prospective validation in cohorts with matched neurocognitive data.

title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Single-Cell Analysis Prioritizes YWHAB Within Ubiquitination-Related Transcriptional Programs in Endometrial Carcinoma.
abstract: Ubiquitination-related transcriptional programs may help characterize epithelial heterogeneity in endometrial carcinoma (EC). We aimed to identify candidates associated with these programs and epithelial plasticity. We integrated a 43,613-cell atlas from five endometrioid EC samples and two normal endometrial samples with bulk transcriptomic, genetic-association and protein-expression data. Five scoring methods defined a consensus expression score, with HIGH and LOW quartiles defined within the Epithelial + EMT_like lineage. Differential expression and high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) identified candidates for exploratory Mendelian randomization (MR) and survival-based prioritization among 541 patients from The Cancer Genome Atlas Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma (TCGA-UCEC) cohort. Repeated nested cross-validation and cross-model feature support were used to evaluate internal performance and candidate stability. Pseudobulk, independently curated ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) gene sets and scSurv input masking provided sensitivity analyses. The lineage-restricted screen identified 444 candidates, including 412 detectable in TCGA. GeneCards and curated Reactome and KEGG UCell scores were positively correlated (ρ = 0.519 and 0.579). YWHAB ranked fourth among 412 genes in the top-10% workflow analysis and fifth in the top-20% sensitivity analysis. Among the 12 nominal MR-associated genes, it had the highest machine-learning priority. Its single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) MR estimate was nominal (odds ratio (OR) = 1.732, p = 0.0488) and did not survive multiple-testing correction. Higher bulk YWHAB expression was associated with poorer overall survival (HR = 2.188, 95% CI 1.559-3.072). Western blotting showed higher YWHAB protein expression in EC than controls (nine versus nine tissues, p = 0.0027), consistent with descriptive Human Protein Atlas (HPA) staining. Single-cell analyses associated YWHAB with RNA processing, proteostasis-related expression and epithelial-state heterogeneity. Lineage-restricted discovery and cross-model prioritization identify YWHAB as an exploratory candidate associated with ubiquitination-related transcriptional programs in EC. Protein-expression evidence supports its further investigation, while causal function and clinical prognostic utility require independent validation.

title: TOP2A Overexpression as a Prognostic Biomarker in High-Grade Meningioma: An Integrated Single-Cell and Bulk Transcriptomic Study.
abstract: While prior single-cell studies have identified proliferative neoplastic subpopulations, the prognostic and therapeutic implications of TOP2A focal copy-number status have not been defined. This study aimed to delineate the cellular architecture of high-grade meningioma and to evaluate the clinical and prognostic significance of TOP2A expression together with its focal copy-number status through integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic profiling. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was integrated with bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) to resolve the cellular landscape of high-grade meningioma in an exploratory cohort, followed by functional subcluster identification, differential expression analysis, and survival analyses. TOP2A was prioritized for multi-level validation: mRNA overexpression was confirmed in an independent bulk cohort, protein overexpression by immunohistochemistry (IHC), and focal gene copy-number status by fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was performed to evaluate patient prognosis. Correlations between continuous variables were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient. scRNA-seq of an exploratory high-grade cohort revealed a cell-cycle proliferation cluster characterized by high TOP2A expression. In a 160-sample bulk RNA-seq cohort, TOP2A was overexpressed in high-grade and recurrent tumors, and elevated TOP2A mRNA was significantly associated with shorter progression-free survival (PFS). IHC on 154 specimens confirmed TOP2A protein overexpression, and FISH on 27 specimens demonstrated focal TOP2A copy-number gain enriched in high-grade cases. Copy-number gain was concordant with TOP2A mRNA levels. Although TOP2A mRNA and protein overexpression were each associated with shorter PFS, the limited size of the FISH subset precluded an independent survival analysis by copy-number status. This study identifies TOP2A mRNA and protein overexpression as a prognostic biomarker in high-grade meningioma, and shows that focal TOP2A copy-number gain is enriched in high-grade tumors and concordant with TOP2A expression. By integrating transcriptional overexpression with copy-number gain, our findings identify TOP2A as a candidate prognostic biomarker warranting prospective evaluation in high-grade meningioma.
